data.title: Google is burying the web alive
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: Google的AI概览功能通过在搜索结果顶部提供简短回答，试图在用户滚动之前解决查询问题。该功能在去年的开发者大会上正式推出，并被誉为“过去十年搜索最成功的新功能之一”。今年的开发者大会上，Google推出了“AI模式”，这是一个更深刻的改变。与AI概览不同，AI模式完全取代了传统的搜索结果，提供更强大的AI搜索功能，包括更深层次的推理和多模态响应，并通过后续问题和链接深入探索。尽管该模式提供了类似于ChatGPT的体验，但它更多地将链接作为备份和来源，而非引导用户点击访问外部网站。这一变化反映了Google在自动化和信息处理方面的优先事项，但也引发了关于数据来源和平台间依赖关系的讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google搜索结果中引入AI后对网站和用户的影响

不同观点：
• **nicbou**：运营信息网站多年，流量下降30%，认为AI正取代人类内容创作者，且通过AI生成的内容缺乏细节和人性化。网站主不仅收入受影响，创作乐趣也被剥夺，被迫更多关注商业运营而非内容创作。
• **ninth_ant**：不认为必须使用Google，还有其他搜索引擎如DuckDuckGo可供选择，不必因为Google的产品决策而抱怨整个网络环境被破坏。
• **romaaeterna**：认为现在的变化是在埋葬早已不复从前的网络，隐含对过去网络环境的怀念。
• **Magi604**：起初不喜欢AI概述，但逐渐习惯，认为AI概述比筛选大量SEO优化垃圾网站更有效率。
• **almusdives**：认为AI对依赖高流量的广告行业不利，但对于提供实际服务的网站影响不大，用户最终找到所需服务即可。
• **NewsaHackO**：支持AI引入，认为可以减少低质量的SEO网站，提升搜索体验。
• **kazinator**：提出在查询中添加特定词语可以避免讨厌的AI总结，表明用户仍有方法绕过AI内容。
• **bilater**：认为Google必须拥抱AI以避免“创新者困境”，尽管会惹恼部分用户，但这是唯一的前进道路。
• **AriedK**：担心企业可能通过付费影响AI系统推荐，提出对商业化可能的担忧。
• **Rastonbury**：希望Google展示用户指定来源的结果而非AI总结，认为搜索引擎结果质量下降，因此转向ChatGPT，但对其不完全信任。
• **kevin_thibedeau**：因常规搜索引擎偏向近期内容和电商网站，不得不使用ChatGPT查找历史信息。
• **rambambram**：认为不必担心网络消失，强调不应被“开放网络已死”的论调误导，线下营销同样有效。
• **carlosjobim**：认为出版商多年前本可以通过联合订阅解决当前困境，但因内部政治分歧未能实现，YouTube的成功案例表明合作的重要性。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Google引入AI对内容创作者的影响，部分人认为AI提高了搜索效率，而内容创作者和部分用户则担心AI破坏了网络生态和收入来源。
• **搜索引擎选择**：部分用户提出可以选择其他搜索引擎以避免Google的产品决策影响，但也有用户质疑整个网络是否正在被少数公司控制。
• **商业化担忧**：有人担心AI搜索结果的商业化可能导致付费推荐，影响搜索公正性。
• **历史对比**：一些用户对过去网络环境的怀念和对当前变化的批评，反映出对网络演变的复杂情感。

44097490.article_content:
Photo-Illustration: Intelligencer
By now, there’s a good chance you’ve encountered
Google
’s
AI Overviews
, possibly thousands of times. Appearing as blurbs at the top of search results, they attempt to settle your queries before you scroll — to offer answers, or relevant information, gleaned from websites that you no longer need to click on. The feature was officially rolled out at Google’s developer conference last year and had been in testing for quite some time before that; on the occasion of this year’s conference, the company characterized it as “one of the most successful launches in Search in the past decade,” a strangely narrow claim that is almost certainly true: Google put AI summaries on top of everything else,
for everyone,
as if to say, “Before you use our main product, see if this works instead.”
This year’s conference included another change to search, this one more profound but less aggressively deployed. “AI Mode,” which has similarly been in beta testing for a while, will appear as an option for all users. It’s not like AI Overviews; that is, it’s not an extra module taking up space on a familiar search-results page but rather a complete replacement for conventional search. It’s Google’s “most powerful AI search, with more advanced reasoning and multimodality, and the ability to go deeper through follow-up questions and helpful links to the web,” the company says, “breaking down your question into subtopics and issuing a multitude of queries simultaneously on your behalf.” It’s available to everyone. It’s a lot like using AI-first chatbots that have search functions, like those from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Perplexity, and Google says it’s destined for greater things than a small tab. “As we get feedback, we’ll graduate many features and capabilities from AI Mode right into the core Search experience,” the company says.
I’ve been testing AI Mode for a few months now, and in some ways it’s less radical than it sounds and (at first) feels. It resembles the initial demos of AI search tools, including those by Google, meaning it responds to many questions with clean, ad-free answers. Sometimes it answers in extended plain language, but it also makes a lot of lists and pulls in familiar little gridded modules — especially when you ask about things you can buy — resulting in a product that, despite its chatty interface, feels an awful lot like … search.
Again, now you can try it yourself, and your mileage may vary; it hasn’t drawn me away from Google proper for a lot of thoughtless rote tasks, but it’s competitive with
ChatGPT
for the expanding range of searchish tasks you might attempt with a chatbot.
From the very first use, however, AI Mode crystallized something about Google’s priorities and in particular its relationship to the web from which the company has drawn, and returned, many hundreds of billions of dollars of value. AI Overviews demoted links, quite literally pushing content from the web
down
on the page, and summarizing its contents for digestion without clicking:
Photo-Illustration: Intelligencer; Screenshot: Google
Meanwhile, AI Mode all but
buries
them, not just summarizing their content for reading within Google’s product but inviting you to explore and expand on those summaries by asking more questions, rather than clicking out. In many cases, links are retained merely to provide backup and sourcing, included as footnotes and appendices rather than destinations:
Photo-Illustration: Intelligencer; Screenshot: Google
This is typical with AI search tools and all but inevitable now that such things are possible.
In terms of automation
, this means companies like OpenAI and Google are mechanizing some of the “work” that goes into using tools like Google search, removing, when possible, the step where users leave their platforms and reducing, in theory, the time and effort it takes to navigate to somewhere else when necessary. In even broader terms — contra Google’s effort to brand this as “going beyond information to intelligence” — this is an example of how LLMs offer
different ways to interact with much of the same information
: summarization rather than retrieval, regeneration rather than fact-finding, and vibe-y reconstruction over deterministic reproduction.
This is interesting to think about and often compelling to use but leaves unresolved one of the
first questions
posed by chatbots-as-search: Where will they get all the data they need to
continue
to work well? When Microsoft and Google showed off their first neo-search mockups in 2023, which are pretty close to today’s AI mode, it revealed
a dilemma
:
Search engines still provide the de facto gateway to the broader web, and have a deeply codependent relationship with the people and companies whose content they crawl, index, and rank; a Google that instantly but sometimes unreliably summarizes the websites to which it used to send people would destroy that relationship, and probably a lot of websites, including the ones on

data.title: Year 2038 Problem
data.author: abixb
data.article_summary: The Year 2038 problem (Y2038) is a time computation issue that affects systems using 32-bit signed integers to store Unix time, which counts seconds since January 1, 1970. At 03:14:08 UTC on January 19, 2038, these systems will encounter an integer overflow, causing them to misinterpret the date as December 13, 1901. This is due to the limited range of a 32-bit integer, which can only represent times between 1901 and 2038. The issue is similar to the Y2K problem but involves binary numbers. Systems using 64-bit integers are not affected, as their overflow point is far beyond practical time scales. epoch

before

year 2000 problem

base 10 numbers

base 2 numbers
.
Analogous storage constraints will be reached in

age of the universe

(ABS),

(ESC/ESP),
traction control

four-wheel drive
; aircraft may use
inertial guidance systems
and
GPS receivers
.

data.title: Reflections on Neuralese
data.author: tie-in
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了神经网络中的潜在空间推理（Neuralese）对大型语言模型（LLM）可解释性的影响。随着链式思维（Chain of Thought, CoT）推理的突破，研究人员尝试让LLM在潜在空间中进行推理，而不是依赖于 token。这种方法被称为 Neuralese，其目的是提高推理效率，减少所需的推理 token 数量。然而，Neuralese 的推理过程难以直接解释，因为它不通过传统的投影和采样步骤，而这些步骤原本有助于理解模型的推理过程。

Neuralese 提供了更高的信息带宽，但其高维度和稀疏性使得从 token 角度解释其语义结构变得困难。文章指出，理解和翻译 Neuralese 的信息需要新的技术和方法，以应对这种新型推理带来的可解释性挑战。

Reflections on Neuralese
Alice Blair

27
points
0
comments
5
min read
LW
link
AI
Interpretability (ML & AI)
Thanks to Brendan Halstead for feedback on an early draft of this piece. Any mistakes here are my own.
[Epistemic status: I’ve looked at
the relevant code
enough to be moderately sure I understand what’s going on. Predictions about the future, including about what facts will turn out to be relevant, are uncertain as always.]
Introduction
With the
recent breakthroughs
taking advantage of extensive Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning in LLMs, there have been many attempts to modify the technique to be even more powerful. One of the natural ideas for improving CoT is to have LLMs perform CoT reasoning in the same latent space that they use for reasoning within a single forward pass, rather than being constrained to the space of possible tokens.
However, as people working on AI safety, it makes sense to ask how this changes the game for LLM interpretability. After all, we
are able
to catch a large fraction of current LLM deception by monitoring their natural-language CoT, since right now CoT is primarily faithful to the LLM’s true reasoning and is legible to us given the right techniques. In order to understand this strategic situation, it’s important to understand this new “language” (which people often refer to as Neuralese) that is created by reasoning in latent spaces instead of using tokens.
Understanding Neuralese
To refresh, a language transformer starts by embedding input tokens as vectors in some high-dimensional latent space, and runs each of these embeddings through a series of repeated computational layers. Then, of the resulting modified vectors in latent space, the vector that previously corresponded to the final input token is projected and normalized to create a probability distribution over what the next token could be. Then, to actually get the next token, you sample from the distribution.
Chain of Thought reasoning works so well because the model does some computation, outputs a token, and then all future instances of that model have access to that information as well. In essence, this technique for storing information between different forward passes greatly increases the serial depth of computation that is possible for the model. Because there is a computation in latent space corresponding to every input token, the computation also gets wider as the model reasons more, allowing for more parallelized reasoning
[1]
.
The recent
Neuralese paper
takes this process and removes a few steps. It notices that the projection and sampling process loses almost all of the information encoded in the last layer of the model, and to increase the bandwidth of information flowing through the reasoning process, you can simply remove that lossy part of the computation. Instead, they have the model directly output the aforementioned high-dimensional latent vector without projecting it, and then that is used as an embedding for the model in future steps:
After training the model (GPT-2 small) to take advantage of the new Neuralese modality, we can see significant decreases in the number of reasoning tokens needed to achieve roughly equivalent performance, from around
1
⁄
3
to
1
⁄
10
of the original number:
Compare CoT and COCONUT (aka Neuralese)
It’s unclear how much these results line up with expectations and theoretical limits, since it’s hard to tell how lossy the removed computations are and how effective this type of training can be at taking advantage of the extra efficiency. At the extreme theoretical limit for GPT-2, the normal CoT paradigm outputs at most
log
2
(
vocabulary_size
)
≈
15.6
bits
per token, and the new paradigm outputs at most
embedding_dimension
×
floating_point_precision
=
24576
bits per token, but there are numerous reasons to expect that this ratio doesn’t hold on practical implementations
[2]
.
Interpreting Neuralese
Natural-language CoT interpretability differs from Neuralese CoT interpretability in a number of key ways:
Necessarily, Neuralese vectors are only useful when they are encoding information that isn’t preserved through the projection and sampling steps, so we can’t interpret the full breadth of information in Neuralese vectors as tokens by using those usual methods. Thus, we are not able to naively interpret the reasoning behind the gained capabilities of the Neuralese reasoner, even if we are able to understand some lossily compressed version of that reasoning using projection and sampling.
There are many semantic structures not compactly represented by tokens available: given the high dimensionality of the latent space, token embeddings are very sparse within it and there is thus a large amount of space which is compactly expressible in latent vectors but not in existing tokens. A useful concept for an LLM using Neuralese reasoning may be extremely difficult to translate because of this sparsity
[3]
.

主要讨论点：在大语言模型（LLM）或AI API交互中，如何有效地管理、存储和传递上下文（context）以获得更好的输出。

不同观点：
• **esafak**：认为MCP（可能是Model-Context-Prompt）是声明上下文管理API的合适位置，建议构建一个通用的上下文存储，将上下文更贴近模型。
• **matt_s**：强调与LLM交互类似于调用函数，提供调优后的输入能获得更好的输出。提到如果需要跨用户会话保存状态，数据库是常见选择，也可以使用文件存储，非网页开发环境可使用sqlite。
• **coolKid721**：主张通过定制化提示（prompts）传递相关上下文，认为没有捷径。分享了使用Elixir Phoenix和GenServer管理用户状态的经验，并强调每次交互都是独特的，需要实验以找到最佳输出。
• **ProfessorZoom**：描述了一种嵌入信息并保存在数据库中的方法，通过存储过程计算最相关的信息，并在编辑器中展示相关信息，支持实时更新嵌入。
• **max_on_hn**：建议使用分析工具（如Mixpanel、PostHog）在运行时收集原始数据，并通过通用摘要器转换为可用的行为上下文。
• **nico**：表示对此问题尚未解决但很感兴趣，希望有一种像hotjar/analytics脚本的工具自动收集上下文，并能查询生成提示上下文。
• **bilater**：提供了一个可能有用的链接（https://context7.com/）。

补充讨论：
• **barbazoo**：回应nico的评论，再次提到MCP，并建议提供工具让LLM在运行时发现数据。

争议焦点：
• **定制化与通用工具**：coolKid721主张高度定制化和实验以获得最佳结果，而nico和max_on_hn则希望有现成的工具和自动化方案。
• **存储和管理方式**：不同参与者提出了多种存储和管理上下文数据的方法，包括数据库（sqlite、自定义数据库方案）、文件存储以及实时计算和更新嵌入。

总体而言，讨论围绕如何有效管理LLM交互中的上下文展开，涉及定制化提示、状态管理、数据存储方案以及自动化工具的开发和使用。

data.title: Kugelmugel
data.author: _Microft
data.article_summary: **Republic of Kugelmugel**是位于奥地利维也纳的一个微国家，由艺术家Edwin Lipburger于1976年创立。这个微国家基于一个直径8米的球形建筑，最初因未经许可建造而与当局发生争执。Lipburger宣布该建筑为独立国家，甚至发行护照。经过多年的法律纠纷，该建筑于1982年被迁移到维也纳的Prater公园，由时任市长Helmut Zilk给予“庇护”。尽管法律地位未定，维也纳市最终接受其作为城市文化的一部分。Edwin Lipburger于2015年去世，其子Nikolaus继任，2022年Linda Treiber成为总统。Kugelmugel目前拥有超过650名非居民公民，并向游客开放，发放签证。

Kugelmugel
, officially the
Republic of Kugelmugel
(
German
:
Republik Kugelmugel
), is a spherical art object located in
Vienna
,
Austria
.
It came about as the result of the artist Edwin Lipburger constructing the 8 meter diameter spherical object without permissions from the authorities in
Austria
. After the dispute between the artist and authorities, the artist declared it a
micronation
, and it was eventually granted asylum by the then-mayor
Helmut Zilk
in
Vienna
where it is housed in the
Prater
park.
The 'Republic' is currently administered by Linda Treiber as president.
History
[
edit
]
The Republic of Kugelmugel
Front entrance with sign for border crossing (2024)
The interior of the spherical house
In 1971, the 8 meter in diameter building was constructed by Edwin Lipburger and his son Nikolaus in
Katzelsdorf
near Wiener Neustadt in
Lower Austria
. A prolonged dispute between the authorities and Lipburger ensued over the following years over the unpermitted construction.
[
1
]
Lipburger declared Kugelmugel as its own micronation, even issuing passports. In August 1975, the township of
Neudörfl
offered to house the building and discussion of how to transport the building, potentially via helicopter were discussed, but ultimately didn't pan out.
[
2
]
In 1979, Lipburger was sentenced to prison for 10 weeks for "unlawful assumption of a public authority" (
Amtsanmaßung
).
[
3
]
In 1982 the building was taken apart and transported to Vienna in the
Prater
park, near the Hauptallee, and surrounded by eight-foot-tall barbed-wire fences. The house occupies the only address within the proclaimed Republic: "2., Antifaschismusplatz" ("
2nd district
of Vienna; Anti-Fascism Square").
[
3
]
[
1
]
In 1982 the building was officially adopted by the city of Vienna by then-mayor
Helmut Zilk
who granted the object "asylum".
[
4
]
[
5
]
However it was then assumed by the city that the artistic object would only be temporary, so the legal dispute continued on with the city of Vienna after power and water was cut to Kugelmugel. Various lawsuits have been filed subsequently and eventually rose all the way to the
Supreme Administrative Court of Austria
in 2007.
[
6
]
However all lawsuits failed with no formal agreement ever reached between Lipburger and the city. The city has stopped any attempts at reclaiming it and has accepted it as part of Vienna's culture and is allowing the building in its existence as a "building built without a permit" (
Superädifikat

data.title: Why Buy a Camper When You Could Build a Stealthier One Out of Pallets Yourself?
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种自制隐形露营车的方法，灵感来自YouTube用户Steve Wallis的实践。由于传统房车和旅行拖车价格高昂，如最便宜的Airstream房车也要近5万美元，作者建议不如自己用木托盘建造一个更经济的露营车。这种自制露营车外观看似一堆木托盘，能够避免引人注意，解决了传统房车容易暴露有人在住宿的问题。虽然手工制作可能不如高端产品精致，但通过现代电池技术，仍能配备内部照明、安全系统和慢炖锅等设施。这种DIY方式提供了一种经济实惠且灵活的旅行住宿选择，体现了“车居生活”（vanlife）趋势下对高房价的应对策略。

44098640.article_content:
Culture
Wrenching
Why Buy A Camper When You Could Build A Stealthier One Out Of Pallets Yourself?
By
Collin Woodard
May 26, 2025 11:25 am EST
Steve Wallis/YouTube
There's just something about hitting the open road with no need to book a hotel or stay with a friend, because you're hauling your own place to stay for the night. Sure, current hashtag vanlife trends may be motivated by
how ridiculously expensive housing has gotten
, but even before Reagan voters set the U.S. on a path to ruin,
Americans loved their RVs and travel trailers
. The biggest problem, though, is that travel trailers are also ridiculously expensive.
Want an Airstream like you see on TV? Well, the least-expensive Airstream costs nearly $50,000, and the Pottery Barn Special Edition will run you an eye-watering $171,300. That isn't even the most expensive Airstream, either. At that point, you might as well buy one of those stationary condos with an HOA and zero wheels. Wait, actually, I just checked, and the wealthy NIMBYs just blocked the new condos that were supposed to get built. Can't risk their property values, after all.
So if you want a travel trailer but don't have six figures to throw around, are you out of luck? Nope. Just build your own like our friend Steve Wallis did here. It isn't pretty, but that's actually the point.
Stealth camping
As we all know, the second-biggest problem with campers is that, even if you can afford one, everyone immediately knows what they're looking at. They all scream, "Someone's sleeping in here, and they probably have their stuff with them." And cops don't like it when people sleep somewhere without a foundation. Disguise your travel trailer as a stack of wood pallets, though, and there you go. Problem solved. Instead of everyone assuming you're a shifty ne'er-do-well, they'll just think you're headed to a bonfire or a Real American (TM) doing Real Work.
Sure, he could have probably done a slightly better job ensuring the entire setup was watertight, but it's not like the travel trailers and RVs people spend six figures on
have the best reputation there, either
. Plus, it has a skylight. And modern batteries mean it's possible to set up interior lights, an entire security system with exterior cameras and a slow cooker. Just don't let anyone from Louisiana see that Crock-Pot "jambalaya" he makde for dinner, even if it probably tasted better than the vast majority of camping meals. Does Canada have Tony Chachere's? Surely, you can at least get good ole Tony C's up in Canada, Steve.
What are you gonna do while the jambalaya's slow-cooking? Well, that's the great thing about campers. Just walk into a nearby corporate chain restaurant, catch the Canadian Ice Soccer game on one of the many TVs, sip a beer or two, and even if two turns into 12, you've still got a bed within stumbling distance and a pot of warm jambalaya to go back to. If that isn't luxury living, I don't know what is.

data.title: Tech Conferences are ramping up security to quell employee protests
data.author: donsupreme
data.article_summary: 上周谷歌和微软的年度开发者大会上，安全问题成为焦点。在微软Build大会上，便衣保安强行带离抗议员工，这些员工反对微软与以色列政府的合同。同时，谷歌I/O大会的安检也异常严格。科技公司因与政府合作增多，安全需求上升，尤其在人工智能技术快速发展和涉及国防领域的背景下。微软此前也曾遭遇类似抗议，员工要求公司停止与以色列军方的合作。全球威胁解决方案公司CEO指出，当前世界动荡，科技公司的安全措施显著加强。

At annual developer conferences last week for Google and Microsoft, the companies' heightened security concerns were on full display.
Undercover guards were in attendance at Microsoft Build, forcing out protesting employees.
Security firms and experts told CNBC that tech companies have increased security needs as they engage in more sensitive work with governments.

Security officers block entrance doors after pro-Palestinian protesters attempted to enter the Microsoft Build conference at the Seattle Convention Center Arch building in Seattle, Washington on May 19, 2025.
Jason Redmond | Afp | Getty Images
At
Microsoft's
annual Build conference on Tuesday, Executive Vice President Jay Parikh's keynote was interrupted by an employee protesting the company's contracts with the Israeli government. The protester at the Seattle Convention Center was quickly whisked away by security guards, including some undercover agents dressed like attendees.
More than 800 miles south in Mountain View, California, security guards lined the mainstage of Google I/O, where
Alphabet
CEO
Sundar Pichai
was set to speak. At the entrance to the developers conference, roughly two dozen black-clad guards rifled through bags, opening up lipstick cases and pulling out items, including women's feminine products, and confiscating over-the-counter pain medications.
The vibe is different during this year's tech conference season. Tensions were already elevated after the October 2023 attack by Hamas on Israel and the extended bombing campaign in the Gaza Strip that followed. But they've heightened in recent months as artificial intelligence technologies advance at a rapid rate and an AI arms race has entered the most sensitive parts of society.
Additionally, there's the aftermath of the
fatal shooting
in December of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in midtown Manhattan as the executive was on way on his way to an investor event.
"We definitely have seen an uptick in the request for security, specifically in the last six to nine months," said Richard Dossett, client relations manager for American Global Security, which works with tech companies. "There have also been a lot of protests and civil upheaval, especially in Fortune 500 companies, with the landscape at the moment, so they want extra security to make sure they're not going to be hassled."
Security firms and industry experts told CNBC that technology companies' increased work with governments has contributed to an uptick in security needs. AI companies in recent months have been
walking back
bans on military use of their products and entering into deals with defense industry giants and the Defense Department.
Companies are responding to increased outrage in part by trying to quell internal dissent. Google last year
expanded
its list of prohibited discussion topics to include international issues, territorial disputes, national policy events and military conflicts.
A demonstrator is removed from the audience as they interrupt a presentation by Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella at the Microsoft Build 2025 conference in Seattle, Washington on May 19, 2025.
Jason Redmond | AFP | Getty Images
For Microsoft, this week's protests had recent precedent.
In April, former employees
interrupted
the company's 50th anniversary celebrations, calling Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman a "war profiteer." Ibtihal Aboussad, then a software engineer in the company's AI division, walked toward the stage at the event in Redmond, Washington saying, "You claim that you care for using AI for good, but Microsoft sells AI weapons to the Israeli military."
Employees at the company had previously formed a group called
No Azure for Apartheid
, following the creation of similar movements at Google and
Amazon
directed at opposing work with the Israeli government.
Parikh, who runs the newly created CoreAi group at Microsoft, heard that specific message during his Build speech this week.
"Jay!" yelled the worker from the audience. "How dare you talk about AI when my people are suffering! Cut ties! No Azure for apartheid!
CEO
Satya Nadella
was
interrupted
during his keynote by an employee named Joe Lopez.
"Satya! How about you show how Microsoft is killing Palestinians?" Lopez screamed. "How about you show the Israeli war crimes are powered by Azure."
Another employee followed, "As a Microsoft worker, I refuse to be complicit in this genocide. Free Palestine!" That employee was later fired, as was Lopez.
'Turbulent world'
Kenneth Bombace, CEO of Global Threat Solutions, said tech companies "have had robust security but I would say it has picked up in the last year or so, or even more recently."

I Think It's Time to Give Nix a Chance
The modern developer tooling ecosystem has exploded with choices, leading to frustrating scenarios where some piece of code builds perfectly on someoneâs system, runs flawlessly in production, but mysteriously fails to build for you and you have absolutely no idea why. Youâre left debugging with no clear directionâperhaps itâs a missing system dependency, a subtly different library version, or some environment variable that exists somewhere in the void, and nowhere else.
If this sounds familiar, you too might be experiencing the fundamental problem that Nix was designed to solve: the lack of true reproducibility in software development.
Despite being around for about two decades, Nix has largely flown under the radar of mainstream development. Most developers have heard of it in passingâoften described as âthat functional package manager with a steep learning curveâ or âthe thing NixOS usesââdismissing it as academic or overly complex. I believe this perception is getting increasingly outdated, Nix
deserves
a chance.
First, letâs get this out of the way: Nix still
does
have a steep learning curve. It requires learning a new functional programming language, understanding unfamiliar concepts like derivations and the
/nix/store
, and rethinking how package management works. The documentation can be dense, scattered, and the error messages are outright unhelpful in some cases. Youâre essentially learning an entirely different approach to software deployment and environment management.
But hereâs the thingâas of this post, the tooling around Nix has matured significantly, and the problems Nix solves have only become more pressing. If youâve ever lost hours debugging environment differences, juggled multiple version managers, or struggled with reproducible builds, Nix addresses these pain points at the architectural level rather than through workarounds.
And I am here to argue that despite the quirks and learning investment, Nixâs benefits are compelling enough to warrant your time. The question isnât whether Nix, as a tool and a language, is complexâ
it is
. The question is whether the problems it solves are worth learning something genuinely different. In this post, you can expect a brief introduction to what Nix, the tool, can do for you and how it may be worth giving a try right now.
Why Traditional Package Management Breaks Down
Most package managers work by installing software into shared system locations. Install a specific version of Python, and it goes straight into
/usr/bin/python
. Need a different version of Python for another project? You either overwrite the first installation or create complex alternatives systems that are painful to manage.
This shared-state approach creates inevitable conflicts:
Your frontend application needs the latest version of NodeJS, but a legacy service requires an older one.
Your applications depend on conflicting versions of OpenSSL libraries.
Teams use different operating systems with slightly different utilities. Heck, even same versions of tools, like
sed
, are functionally different across Linux and MacOS.
In such cases, one may say that version managers help with language runtimes. But what about system libraries, databases, or compiled tools? You end up juggling multiple such tools, each with different commands and behaviors.
Orchestration and containerized solutions like Docker and Kubernetes help, but they introduce their own complexities and performance downgrades. More importantly, Docker containers themselves arenât reproducibleârunning
apt-get update
or
pip install requests
at different times can yield different results, even with the same Dockerfile. And frankly, no one really needs Kubernetes, they just have it because everyone and their grandma has it. I digress, thatâs a topic for another day.
This is where Nix comes in.
â¦And How Nix Solves the Problem
Nix makes no assumptions about the global state of your system and takes a fundamentally different approach. Instead of installing packages into shared locations where they can conflict, everything goes into the immutable
/nix/store
, with each package getting a unique directory based on a cryptographic hash of its build inputs.
/nix/store/2v66xkgfmdipzpwgl813n4mqgck6w3fd-nodejs-22.14.0/
/nix/store/2znhzcp5ran8q5mzyqgz6lxi3a56rgva-nodejs-20.18.1/
/nix/store/4rk85a5rsladhcc3ffpnx2kwglvs0i-nodejs-18.17.0/
These hashes are computed using SHA-256 over the packageâs complete build dependency graphâsource code, compiler version, build flags, dependencies, even the build script itself. Change any input, and you get a different hash, which means a completely separate package in the store.
Cryptographic Guarantees and Safety
Technically, you might state that hash collisions are possible with any cryptographic hash function, and you wonât be wrong here. However, the probability of a SHA-2

data.title: How I found a Star Wars website made by the CIA
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 这篇文章由Ciro Santilli撰写，披露了CIA在2000年代末至2010年代初用于秘密通信的网站网络。这些网站被伊朗和中国等国家的反情报部门发现，导致多名线人被捕或处决，最终迫使CIA关闭该通信渠道。文章基于2022年路透社的一篇报道，通过分析公开信息，找出了数百个疑似属于该网络的网站。这些网站似乎不仅针对敌对国家，还包括德国、法国、西班牙和巴西等民主国家。文章详细描述了研究方法和结果，并呼吁公众进一步发现和验证其他可能的网站。Ciro Santilli的政治立场倾向于支持民主和反对独裁，并对美国外交政策的道德性持怀疑态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于美国中情局（CIA）使用秘密网站与特工通信的讨论，特别是这些网站被揭露后的影响及相关技术问题。

不同观点：
• [impossiblefork] 认为让特工连接到一个小众网站是非常不专业的做法，甚至提到使用Cardan Grille（一种古老的加密方法）加上HN（可能指Hacker News）都比这种方法更可取。该评论者还指出，接受这种通信方式的特工也应该拒绝这种不安全的做法。

• [araes] 提到了一篇路透社的文章，这篇文章揭示了一个名为Iraniangoals.com的网站，该网站表面上是一个足球粉丝网站，实际上隐藏了秘密通信功能。通过简单的右键点击查看网页代码，就能发现隐藏的秘密消息功能。该评论者强调了该网站的糟糕设计以及其带来的安全隐患。

• [Improvement] 提供了更多背景信息，指出这些网站从2000年代末到2010年代初被中情局使用，直到2010-2013年间被目标国家的反情报机构发现。该评论者还提到了一项研究，从路透社的文章出发，发现了更多可能的候选网站，并认为这些网站极有可能属于同一网络。

• [toomuchtodo] 提供了另一个相关的例子，即中情局秘密运营了一个《星球大战》粉丝网站，进一步说明这种做法的广泛性。

• [Michelangelo11] 认为这个话题既引人入胜又令人难以置信，并希望获得更多背景信息以更好地理解整个事件。

• [FridayoLeary] 讨论了这些网站被伊朗和中国反情报机构发现后导致的后果，包括一些特工被监禁和处决。该评论者还提到了一篇关于情报和国防告密者的文章，指出中情局承包商John A. Reidy早在2008年就对这些通信系统的安全性提出了 concerns，但被忽视，最终导致了情报灾难。评论还指出，这个系统被过度扩展使用，原本设计用于短期和简单通信的系统被长期和广泛使用，最终导致失败。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于这种通信方法的不专业性和安全性，特别是让特工连接到小众且不安全的网站是否合理。
• 另一个值得注意的点是这些网站的糟糕设计和其带来的安全隐患，以及这些网站被过度扩展使用导致的灾难性后果。
• 评论中还提到了多篇相关文章和研究，提供了更多背景信息和例子，进一步说明这种做法的广泛性和潜在风险。

44098274.article_summary: 这篇文章由Ciro Santilli撰写，披露了CIA在2000年代末至2010年代初用于秘密通信的网站网络。这些网站被伊朗和中国等国家的反情报部门发现，导致多名线人被捕或处决，最终迫使CIA关闭该通信渠道。文章基于2022年路透社的一篇报道，通过分析公开信息，找出了数百个疑似属于该网络的网站。这些网站似乎不仅针对敌对国家，还包括德国、法国、西班牙和巴西等民主国家。文章详细描述了研究方法和结果，并呼吁公众进一步发现和验证其他可能的网站。Ciro Santilli的政治立场倾向于支持民主和反对独裁，并对美国外交政策的道德性持怀疑态度。

data.title: Chomsky on what ChatGPT is good for (2023)
data.author: mef
data.article_summary: 在2023年5月3日的采访中，著名语言学家诺姆·乔姆斯基讨论了ChatGPT和人工智能（AI）的广泛影响。ChatGPT是基于大型语言模型（LLM）的AI聊天机器人，正在改变各行各业并引发重大伦理问题。乔姆斯基区分了AI的工程应用与科学研究，指出AI工程主要关注实用产品，而科学追求理解生物系统的智能。虽然AI在某些任务上（如国际象棋）已经超越人类，但这并不意味着AI全面超越人类智能。乔姆斯基还警告，当前的LLM技术可能被用于传播虚假信息和误导公众，因此许多AI研究人员呼吁暂停开发以应对潜在风险。技术的潜在好处必须与可能的代价相权衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Chomsky关于LLMs（大型语言模型）与人类智能关系的观点的讨论

不同观点：
• atdt：认为对Chomsky观点的讨论缺乏深度。他指出，LLMs的进步尽管在实用性上巨大，但尚未加深我们对人类智能的理解。同时，LLMs是否会通过小型化等途径揭示出类似人类智能的特性仍是未知数。
• papaver-somnamb：LLMs是纯粹的统计模型，缺乏符号推理能力，无法与Chomsky对智能的定义相符。LLMs虽然复杂且有实际价值，但只是一种“花招”，并不能代表真正的智能。
• visarga：反对Chomsky的观点，认为语言与人类大脑是共同演化的，语言是为了适应人类的能力和需求而发展的，而不是相反。
• Xmd5a：提到Chomsky目前在用Hopf代数研究语言结构，暗示Chomsky的观点可能已经发展或改变。
• r00sty：认为当前LLMs被用于降低劳动成本和获取利润，而非科学发展。如果继续这样，科学进步将停滞。
• zombot：支持r00sty的观点，认为人们被利润和控制欲蒙蔽，忽视了理性讨论。
• teleforce：不同意Chomsky关于人类并非认知能力顶端的观点，认为人类通过科学发现和工程已经超越其他生物，并负有保护这些生物的责任。
• bawana：用“猴子打字”的比喻说明LLMs通过训练和反馈机制可以产生看似智能的回应，但本质上仍是人类创造的工具。
• ashoeafoot：提到ChatGPT可以为暴力政权写辩护词，暗示LLMs可能被用于不道德的目的。
• calibas：认为LLMs将语言翻译成计算机能“理解”的形式，应该让语言学家感到兴奋。LLMs尽管不具备人类意识，但其方法有效，对语言学分析有革命性意义。
• asmeurer：批评Chomsky对LLMs不能告诉我们关于语言的任何信息的观点是基于人类认知定义的拟人化论点。
• lucisferre：引用科幻作品中的例子，说明不同生物的技术发展路径，间接回应teleforce关于人类与其他生物比较的观点。
• ggm：认为Chomsky的观点总是引发两极分化的讨论，同意Chomsky对AGI（人工通用智能）特性的质疑，批评当前对LLMs的误用和缺乏科学方法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Chomsky关于LLMs与人类智能关系的观点引发广泛争议，尤其是LLMs是否具备符号推理能力、是否能加深我们对人类智能的理解，以及LLMs的实用价值与潜在风险。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：LLMs的小型化潜力、Chomsky对语言与大脑共同演化的观点、LLMs的伦理问题和科学发展停滞的担忧。

Noam Chomsky Speaks on What ChatGPT Is Really Good For
Noam Chomsky Interviewed by C.J. Polychroniou
May 3, 2023.
Common Dreams.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is sweeping the world. It is transforming every walk of life and raising in the process major ethical concerns for society and the future of humanity. ChatGPT, which is dominating social media, is an AI-powered chatbot developed by OpenAI. It is a subset of machine learning and relies on what is called Large Language Models that can generate human-like responses. The potential application for such technology is indeed enormous, which is why there are already calls to regulate AI like ChatGPT.
Can AI outsmart humans? Does it pose public threats? Indeed, can AI become an existential threat? The world’s preeminent linguist
Noam Chomsky
, and one of the most esteemed public intellectuals of all time, whose intellectual stature has been compared to that of Galileo, Newton, and Descartes, tackles these nagging questions in the interview that follows.
C. J. Polychroniou
: As a scientific discipline, artificial intelligence (AI) dates back to the 1950s, but over the last couple of decades it has been making inroads into all sort of fields, including banking, insurance, auto manufacturing, music, and defense. In fact, the use of AI techniques has been shown in some instance to surpass human capabilities, such as in a game of chess. Are machines likely to become smarter than humans?
Noam Chomsky
: Just to clarify terminology, the term “machine” here means
program
, basically a theory written in a notation that can be executed by a computer–and an unusual kind of theory in interesting ways that we can put aside here.
We can make a rough distinction between pure engineering and science. There is no sharp boundary, but it’s a useful first approximation. Pure engineering seeks to produce a product that may be of some use. Science seeks understanding. If the topic is human intelligence, or cognitive capacities of other organisms, science seeks understanding of these biological systems.
As I understand them, the founders of AI–Alan Turing, Herbert Simon, Marvin Minsky, and others–regarded it as science, part of the then-emerging cognitive sciences, making use of new technologies and discoveries in the mathematical theory of computation to advance understanding. Over the years those concerns have faded and have largely been displaced by an engineering orientation. The earlier concerns are now commonly dismissed, sometimes condescendingly, as GOFAI–good old-fashioned AI.
Continuing with the question, is it likely that programs will be devised that surpass human capabilities? We have to be careful about the word “capabilities,” for reasons to which I’ll return. But if we take the term to refer to human performance, then the answer is: definitely yes. In fact, they have long existed: the calculator in a laptop, for example. It can far exceed what humans can do, if only because of lack of time and memory. For closed systems like chess, it was well understood in the ‘50s that sooner or later, with the advance of massive computing capacities and a long period of preparation, a program could be devised to defeat a grandmaster who is playing with a bound on memory and time. The achievement years later was pretty much PR for IBM. Many biological organisms surpass human cognitive capacities in much deeper ways. The desert ants in my backyard have minuscule brains, but far exceed human navigational capacities, in principle, not just performance. There is no Great Chain of Being with humans at the top.
The products of AI engineering are being used in many fields, for better or for worse. Even simple and familiar ones can be quite useful: in the language area, programs like autofill, live transcription, google translate, among others. With vastly greater computing power and more sophisticated programming, there should be other useful applications, in the sciences as well. There already have been some: Assisting in the study of protein folding is one recent case where massive and rapid search technology has helped scientists to deal with a critical and recalcitrant problem.
Engineering projects can be useful, or harmful. Both questions arise in the case of engineering AI. Current work with Large Language Models (LLMs), including chatbots, provides tools for disinformation, defamation, and misleading the uninformed. The threats are enhanced when they are combined with artificial images and replication of voice. With different concerns in mind, tens of thousands of AI researchers have recently
called
for a moratorium on development because of potential dangers they perceive.
As always, possible benefits of technology have to be weighed against potential costs.
Quite different questions arise when we turn to AI and science. Here caution is necessary because of exorbitant and reckle

data.author: JadedBlueEyes
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者应对AI爬虫攻击服务器的过程。最初通过设置`robots.txt`和私有仓库减少了爬虫活动，但爬虫随后卷土重来。作者尝试了多种方法，包括使用Traefik的速率限制和CAPTCHA机制，但效果有限。最终，作者采用了`go-away`工具，通过配置规则有效阻止了爬虫请求，同时对合法用户影响较小。虽然CrowdSec也被测试过，但未能有效阻挡爬虫，反而误拦截了作者的正常请求。最终，`go-away`成功解决了爬虫问题，确保了服务器的稳定运行。

44095611.article_content:
Actually stopping AI scrapers from taking down my server
Published on
5/18/2025
by
Jade Ellis
Â·
4 min read
In my
earlier post about Forgejo and scraper bots
, I mentioned that adding a
robots.txt
file helped reduce scraping. Well, it turns out the bots only disappeared because Iâd set the repository to private, and they were receiving numerous 404 errors. They werenât actually respecting
robots.txt
(although Google, at least, was).
Around April 17th, they returned. I set up rate-limiting using Traefikâs built-in middleware, but this traffic wasnât coming from just one or two IPs; it originated from seemingly two entire
/16
blocks within the Alibaba ASN. I configured a Traefik plugin for rate-limiting per IP block, triggering CAPTCHAs when limits were reached. I set a relatively low limit, which initially reduced the request speed. However, this caused issues for automated tools and legitimate users, so I had to increase the rate limit once the request volume subsided enough to prevent further problems.
They returned on May 13th. I was in my exam period and had limited time for countermeasures, so I initially let it be. The next morning, while I was in an exam, the entire server went down. The bots had discovered links to auto-generated source archives and were downloading them at up to 100 Mb/s. Due to how Forgejo generates these archives, this filled up the disk at an alarming rate. Once hundreds of gigabytes of archives consumed all disk space, memory usage also spiked. The combination of disk full errors and high memory pressure took most of my services offline, and databases began failing writes.
Two hours after the server went offline, I regained access, ran the cron job to clean up the archives, and restarted it to ensure system stability. Unfortunately, I was still occupied with exams, but devising a proper mitigation strategy became my top priority.
Early on the 15th, they returned and began downloading ZIP files. They retreated when they started receiving more HTTP 499 errors than 200s. My users noticed the slowdown. This pattern repeated until the 16th, when I finally had time to implement mitigations. Early that morning, their activity became even more aggressive and it had continued throughout the day, providing a live target for testing my mitigations.
The first solution I tried was CrowdSec. I set up the local API and the Traefik bouncer. Unfortunately, the built-in lists had little effect. However, I could now ban IP blocks using their command-line tools. This, however, didnât achieve much, as they switched IPs almost immediately and resumed their activity.
I attempted to set up CrowdSecâs log parsing and scenarios. It seemed to ban a few IPs but was unable to make even a small dent in the attack, despite parsing thousands of log lines per second with numerous âmitigationsâ enabled.
Next, I tried
go-away
(
GitHub
). This tool appeared much more flexible and less likely to disrupt my users than Anubis, a commonly-mentioned tool for PoW checks. I moved the Traefik entrypoints to its container and used the example Forgejo configuration. Immediately, bot requests started receiving 502 errors as they were dropped, while legitimate baseline requests continued to pass through. One of my users reported being blocked; the example configuration blocked multiple ASNs entirely, including one their IP address was within, so I removed that rule. The next spike was met with challenge pages and did not make it through. No other issues with go-away have been reported by my users, and itâs nearly invisible during normal usage.
go-away supports TLS fingerprinting in its rules if HTTPS requests are passed through to it. I briefly experimented with this and successfully got it working. Unfortunately, this came at the cost of request statistics from Traefik and HTTP/3 support, so I disabled it. The author has expressed interest in exposing the module as a Go library for use as a Caddy module. I would be interested in having it as a Traefik plugin to enable integrated fingerprinting without these downsides, offering easier setup and configuration (especially across multiple services) and improved performance. However, I am already very pleased with its effectiveness.
The same cannot be said for CrowdSec; I had left it enabled in the background. Here are some issues it caused:
It blocked my IP because usage of the Matrix client API triggered a âscenarioâ.
It blocked my Forgejo runnerâs IP, which was checking for jobs.
It blocked my Forgejo runner when it attempted to upload a container image.
Meanwhile, it failed to detect a single actual scraper.
It stopped ingesting logs early this morning, and I havenât bothered to fix it yet.

不同观点：
• **pavel_lishin** 认为育儿，特别是头几年，会极大消耗父母的精力和时间。他以自己作为全职在家父亲为例，指出即使他计划在孩子睡觉后和早晨挤出时间写作，育儿的劳累让他难以实现这一目标。他强调没有孩子的人很难理解育儿所耗费的能量。

• **潜在反对观点**（推测可能来自如mitchbob等未直接引用的评论者）：一些人可能认为，只要合理安排时间，即便有孩子，父母依然可以找到足够的时间从事个人爱好或职业工作。这种观点可能认为，虽然育儿确实耗费精力，但通过有效的时间管理和分配，仍然可以兼顾育儿和个人追求。

补充讨论：
• **育儿对时间和精力的实际影响**：pavel_lishin通过亲身经历说明育儿对个人时间的压缩程度，尤其是孩子年幼时，父母难以找到连续的时间段处理其他事务。
• **理解差异**：pavel_lishin指出没有孩子的人可能无法完全理解育儿的辛苦，暗示这种理解差异可能导致外界对全职父母的时间分配有过高期望。
• **争议焦点**：争议的核心在于育儿和个人时间是否真的不可调和，以及是否可以通过时间管理技巧在育儿的同时兼顾个人事业或爱好。这涉及到对育儿责任的认识差异，以及对时间管理能力的不同看法。

data.title: Cloudflare CEO: Football piracy blocks will claim lives
data.author: reynaldi
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了西甲（LaLiga）为了打击盗版，广泛封锁IP地址，导致大量无辜网站受到影响，尤其是通过封锁Cloudflare服务器，波及到众多小型企业和紧急服务资源。Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince警告，这种大范围封锁策略可能导致严重后果，甚至可能危及生命。他指出，紧急服务内容可能因封锁而无法访问，并祈祷不要有人因此丧命。尽管LaLiga将责任归咎于Cloudflare，但Prince表示公司一直愿意与权利持有者合作，通过合法途径保护内容，呼吁政策制定者关注此问题。文章还提到，LaLiga通过法院命令持续进行大规模封锁，引发了对网络自由和用户权利的广泛担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare在西班牙被法院下令封锁所引发的争议，以及关于盗版、内容审核、互联网基础设施集中化等问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持Cloudflare的观点**：
   - SXX认为Cloudflare对抗政府授权的审查和版权组织的滥权是值得尊重的，强调任何云服务都可能被用于不良用途，互联网基础设施提供商不应迎合每个政府的每一个要求。
   - jonhohle提到虽然个人对Cloudflare作为单一入口有顾虑，但其商业使用场景合理。同时指出，如果互联网企业需要承担更多责任，问题将会得到解决。

• **批评Cloudflare及相关措施的观点**：
   - globie批评Cloudflare的CAPTCHA系统对用户不友好，导致用户访问困难，且未对用户进行充分告知。强调Cloudflare的算法可能带来负面影响，特别是在关键服务上。
   - KaiserPro认为Cloudflare不愿下架盗版内容，因此La Liga采取激进措施虽不妥，但也有其背景原因。

• **关于La Liga和盗版问题的观点**：
   - vessenes指出La Liga通过法庭命令封锁Cloudflare IPs的举动是过度的，认为La Liga应像其他版权所有者一样通过发送下架请求来解决问题。
   - jedberg认为La Liga应该通过提高内容的可访问性来解决盗版问题，而不是通过封锁和技术手段。

• **关于技术解决方案和责任分配的观点**：
   - Ekaros建议通过将可信服务与不可信服务分离，并引入巨额经济处罚来防止类似问题。
   - blibble认为互联网基础设施集中于单一入口（如Cloudflare）是一个坏主意，容易成为目标。

• **关于实际影响和用户体验的观点**：
   - Zealotux认为尽管“威胁生命”的叙述有些夸张，但La Liga的封锁行为确实令人难以接受。
   - carlosbaraza分享了自己在西班牙因封锁而遇到的实际问题，包括无法访问公司网站和家庭设备，并提到这对某些依赖互联网设备的用户（如糖尿病患者）可能带来严重后果。

• **关于法律和政府的观点**：
   - Fokamul将问题归咎于西班牙政府和法律，认为这种封锁行为与政府的传统有关，并提到类似法律在其他国家未能通过。

补充讨论：
• 部分讨论者质疑为何其他CDN如CloudFront和Akamai没有遇到类似问题（otterley），这表明Cloudflare可能在某些技术或法律问题上存在特殊性。
• 讨论中还涉及个人技术设置对Cloudflare和CAPTCHA系统体验的影响（jorvi），以及对具体封锁案例（如Vercel）的提及（tough）。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于La Liga通过法院命令封锁整个Cloudflare网络的合理性与合法性，以及Cloudflare在盗版问题上的责任和应对措施。另一个焦点是互联网基础设施集中化带来的潜在风险和解决方案。

Cloudflare CEO: Football Piracy Blocks Will Claim Lives; “I Pray No One Dies”
LaLiga’s 2024/2025 season is officially over. FC Barcelona were actually crowned champions on Thursday after it became mathematically impossible for Real Madrid to conjure up seven points or more from the six points available.
The final matches of the season were played on Sunday but with the championship settled, would LaLiga show restraint and taper down its blocking activity? Or perhaps it would continue under the authority of judge, despite the widespread collateral damage inflicted on innocent internet users since February, a scandal now known as #laligagate.
In For a Penny?
The early signs did little to inspire confidence. Protest website LaLigaGate.com was hit by a total blockade but whether the site was targeted deliberately or succumbed to collateral damage is unknown.
Intentional and Unintentional Blocking Look Identical
As the
latest data
suggests that mass blocking of Cloudflare in pursuit of 150 piracy platforms has negatively affected millions of innocent websites, use of the term ‘collateral damage’ may be running out of scope.
Unintentional overblocking became inevitable overblocking some time ago, a point certainly not lost on Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince.
Posting to X last week, Prince asked if anyone wanted any general feedback, declaring that he felt “in an especially truthful mood.” The first
response
contained direct questions about the LaLiga controversy, the blame for which LaLiga places squarely on the shoulders of Cloudflare.
For the first time since Cloudflare legal action
failed to end LaLiga’s blocking campaign
, Prince weighed in with his assessment of the current situation and where he believes it’s inevitably heading.
“Bonkers” Blocking Strategy
“A huge percentage of the Internet sits behind us, including small businesses and emergency resources in Spain,” Prince explained.
“The strategy of blocking broadly through ISPs based on IPs is bonkers because so much content, including emergency services content, can be behind any IP.
The collateral damage is vast
and is hurting Spanish citizens from accessing critical resources,” he added.
Earlier this year, various comments and statements by LaLiga suggested that its relationship with Cloudflare had reached rock bottom. It transpired that LaLiga had
obtained an injunction
which allowed it to tackle Cloudflare and
Encrypted Client Hello (ECH)
, but had done so without Cloudflare’s knowledge, effectively denying the company a right to respond.
Alongside other attacks delivered via the media, LaLiga slammed Cloudflare for refusing to cooperate. What action LaLiga had demanded still isn’t clear, but the league said that if there was any overblocking as a result, Cloudflare would have to shoulder the blame.
The Potential for Deadly Consequences
The scale of overblocking reported in Spain is unprecedented but since LaLiga has a court order that effectively gives Cloudflare blocking a green light, it has been doing so in bulk, every single week since February.
Depending on who addresses the overblocking issue, with whom and when, the league claims that collateral damage a) doesn’t exist or is minimal and/or b) is Cloudflare’s responsibility. Prince appears to have grave concerns over the scale and type of blocking taking place, warning that a worst-case scenario is inevitable.
Football Piracy Blocks Will Claim Lives
Despite LaLiga’s unshakable claims to the contrary, Prince believes that it’s not a case of ‘if’ disaster strikes, it’s ‘when’.
“It’s only a matter of time before a Spanish citizen can’t access a life-saving emergency resource because the rights holder in a football match refuses to send a limited request to block one resource versus a broad request to block a whole swath of the Internet,” Prince warned.
“When that unfortunately and inevitably happens and harms lives, I’m confident policy makers and courts in Spain and elsewhere will make the right policy decision. Until then, it’ll be up to users to make politicians clear on the risk. I pray no one dies.”
The suggestion that LaLiga’s demands were too broad, doesn’t mean that Cloudflare is refusing to help, Prince suggested. On the contrary, there’s a process available, LaLiga just needs to use it.
“We’ve always been happy and willing to work with rights holders in conjunction with judicial bodies to protect their content. We have a clear process that works around the world to do that, Prince explained.
LaLiga Targeted Cloudflare and Others During the Weekend
Live blocking data provided by
hayahora.futbol
has proven invaluable to those documenting #laligagate in recent months and this past weekend was no different.
As the small sample of Cloudflare IP addresses blocked on Sunday seems to show, concerns that every IP address blocked would inevitably result in collateral damage, seem to have been trumped by the authority of the now-famous court order.

主要讨论点：对一篇文章或新闻报道内容的讨论，主要围绕科技行业的状况、经济环境对科技公司的影响以及投资策略。

不同观点：
• **观点一**：[mitchbob] 认为科技行业正处于一个艰难的时期，尤其是考虑到当前的经济环境和投资者的风险规避态度。他引用了WSJ的一篇文章，指出很多科技公司正面临增长放缓和估值下调的压力。他强调，当前并不是投资科技行业的最佳时机，因为市场情绪普遍低落。

• **观点二**：另一位讨论者（未具名）则认为，尽管当前科技行业面临挑战，但这正是寻找优质投资机会的好时机。他指出，经济低迷时期往往能筛选出真正有实力的公司，并为长期投资者提供良好的入场机会。他以历史上的经济危机为例，说明一些科技巨头正是在经济困境中崛起的。

• **观点三**：还有讨论者（未具名）对科技行业的细分领域表达了不同看法。他认为，并非所有科技子行业都面临同样的困境。例如，人工智能和云计算领域仍然具有较高的增长潜力，值得投资者关注。他强调，选择正确的子行业和公司是关键。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：争议的焦点在于当前经济环境下科技行业是否具有投资价值。一方认为市场情绪低落，投资风险高；另一方则认为经济低迷正是投资的好时机，尤其是对于优质公司和增长潜力大的子行业。

• **论据和例子**：
  - [mitchbob] 引用了WSJ的文章来支持其观点，强调市场整体情绪和科技公司的困境。

data.author: rh3939
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了一个名为 "new_bloom_filter_repo" 的代码库，由用户 "ross39" 创建并公开。该库目前有23个星标（Star），但尚未被其他开发者 fork（复制）。文章还提到，要更改通知设置，用户必须登录。文中没有详细描述代码库的具体功能或内容，仅提供了关于其基本状态的信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新提出的基于Bloom过滤器的视频帧差异压缩方法的可行性、有效性及其应用场景。

不同观点：
• [antirez] 支持该方法，认为它通过将变化的像素位置用位图表示并加入Bloom过滤器，可以有效地压缩视频帧间差异，并通过存储变化的像素数据来重建下一帧。他还提出可以通过设置标记进一步压缩。
• [meatmanek] 质疑该方法在处理原始视频输入时的有效性，认为该方法依赖于像素在连续帧间变化不大的假设，而这在处理未压缩的真实世界视频信号时可能不成立，尤其是存在噪声的情况下。
• [meindnoch] 对该方法的实际效果持怀疑态度，指出根据提供的图表，新方法在压缩率上并不如GZIP。
• [bob1029] 关注压缩比的具体数据，询问是否有不同情况下的压缩比示例，并建议将图片示例加入README以方便理解。
• [Dwedit] 提到H.264可以运行在无损模式，但实际中几乎不使用。
• [vintermann] 认为对于稀疏的二进制字符串，传统方法可能比新方法更好。
• [oivey] 指出新方法的压缩比计算只是基于像素差异的减少，但更重要的比较应该是与压缩后的YouTube视频帧的平均字节大小相比，才能判断是否为改进。
• [hxtk] 对代码中的某一行表示困惑，认为这可能导致压缩变得有损，并丢弃一些像素变化信息。
• [chungy] 对README中提到的“YouTube视频”和“无损视频”感到困惑，询问该方法是针对重新压缩已下载的YouTube视频还是针对从源制作新视频。
• [less_less] 建议考虑使用二进制融合过滤器或类似方法来避免Bloom过滤器的空间使用问题。
• [ggm] 关注该方法的计算成本、是否适用于流处理、压缩比是否在现代数据流中可接受，以及是否为已知的压缩子类并可能受到限制。
• [mxfh] 质疑无损压缩在消费级应用中的意义，尤其是对已经过YouTube转码器处理的视频，并分享了个人在视频归档方面的经验。
• [ambicapter] 对项目的核心目标提出疑问，询问该项目是关于视频压缩还是Bloom过滤器的创新。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于该方法在处理真实世界视频信号时的有效性、压缩比的具体数据及其与现有方法（如GZIP、H.264）的比较。
• 讨论中还涉及到对无损压缩在实际应用中的意义和价值的不同看法。
• 有人建议使用其他过滤器方法来提高空间使用效率，并关注计算成本和流处理的可行性。
• 对代码实现中的某些细节存在疑问，特别是关于是否会导致压缩变得有损。
• 对项目文档的清晰度和示例的提供也提出了改进建议。

data.title: Trying to teach in the age of the AI homework machine
data.author: notarobot123
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在人工智能（AI）日益普及的时代，教育领域面临的挑战，特别是学生利用AI完成作业的问题。作者借用《沙丘》中的Butlerian Jihad原则——“汝不可造出模仿人类心智的机器”——来表达对AI的反对，并指出这种反对不仅是对技术的抵制，更是一种深层次的、近乎精神层面的厌恶。文章提到，越来越多的人，包括作家和艺术家，认为与大型语言模型（LLM）的任何接触都是对创意群体的背叛。

在教育领域，尽管有人希望AI能成为一种无限耐心的数字导师，帮助学生学习，但实际中，AI往往导致学生依赖其完成作业，削弱了真正的学习过程。教师们担心AI让学生跳过那些促进深度学习的“必要困难”，从而影响教育效果。这种现象引发了对AI在教育中应用的广泛担忧和反对。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在教育中的影响以及如何应对

不同观点：
• **支持限制AI使用，回归传统评估方式**：
   - [math_dandy] 认为应回归笔试和监考考试，但管理层希望所有评估都是远程友好型的，以支持在线课程。笔试评估被认为威胁到在线课程的收入增长。
   - [djoldman] 建议增加面对面考试的频率，以防止学生依赖AI作弊。
   - [mrbonner] 支持传统的蓝书式考试，认为这是防止作弊的有效方法。

• **支持合理利用AI，调整教学内容**：
   - [czhu12] 认为AI可以作为个人导师，帮助学习新技能，但在学校环境中可能成为拐杖。
   - [bosuanzi] 认为教育应随时代变化，教师应调整教学内容，帮助学生通过AI更好地掌握相关科目。
   - [esafak] 建议让学生使用AI学习，但通过不允许使用AI的考试验证他们的真实水平。

• **担忧AI导致学生失去独立思考能力**：
   - [sshine] 指出学生将AI当作作业解答器，而不是 tutor，导致他们失去独立思考的习惯。
   - [Aziell] 担心学生逐渐失去思考能力，不仅在学校，在工作中也是如此。

• **对AI在未来教育中的潜力持乐观态度**：
   - [jumploops] 认为AI可以激发学生的好奇心，帮助他们探索更多知识领域，类似于蒙特梭利教学法。
   - [jamesgill] 提出在竞争激烈的世界里，需要思考人类和人类经验的价值，但同时也承认AI的潜力。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否允许学生在学习过程中使用AI，以及如何平衡技术进步与教育质量。
• **具体建议**：增加面对面测试、调整教学内容、利用AI作为学习辅助工具而非替代品。
• **现实问题**：在线课程的收入驱动与传统评估方式之间的冲突。

Trying to teach in the age of the AI homework machine.

“Dover” (1975) by Deborah Remington, giving HAL 9000 vibes in the Phoenix Art Museum
Last summer I
made the case
for bringing the principle of
Dune
’s Butlerian Jihad — “Thou shalt not make a machine in the likeness of a human mind” — to our broader discourse on AI. It seemed like a good way to bind together the various felt and thought objections to AI into a common credo. And a good way to distinguish between benign forms of so-called “AI” (spotting tumors, for instance) and the
sycophantic
imitations of humanity being peddled by the various broligarchs.
Since then, this “hard no” movement against AI has started to take shape. For one the
t-shirt game
keeps getting better.
Traps are being set
on the internet to punish AI scrapers and poison datasets. The
new Chicago pope bashed AI
in his first big speech. Just in my literary corner of the world, anti-AI clauses are becoming standard in book contracts and magazine submission forms. A recent episode of AppleTV’s
The Studio
ended with a crowd at ComicCon — and Ice Cube — chanting “fuck AI.” Last week there was a
WorldCon kerfuffle
(sigh) over using ChatGPT in part of the panel selection process.
(My WorldCon take is that, well intentioned though it was, feeding an AI a list of names and asking it to compile dossiers of their scandals and transgressions is a pretty dystopian use-case.)
It’s clear that writers, artists, and others in that orbit increasingly view any amount of engagement with LLMs as a betrayal of creative class solidarity. The sentiment (which I’ve heard all the way from Tumblr teens to Pulitzer Prize winners) seems to be something like this:
A famous panel from Frank Miller’s
The Dark Knight Returns
.
I’ve heard pushback about such anti-AI puritanism, the ways it’s just another case of social media mob culture. For me, this is where the Butlerian Jihad continues to be a fruitful metaphor. The
Dune
books are all about how holy wars and revolutions are not gentle or reasonable, how they can turn ugly, righteousness fueling a fire that can consume nations and worlds.
The other way the metaphor is proving apt is the deep-seated, almost spiritual nature of anti-AI sentiment. It’s not just more Luddism. Many people — though hardly all, given the popularity of AI products — sense that there is something grotesque about these simulacra, the people who push them on us, this whole affair. That aversion to the technological profane holds even when various stated objections to AI are supposedly addressed or nitpicked to death.
1
Meanwhile, throughout all this, I have myself felt on the front lines of something like a grand struggle against these likeness machines —  not just as a creative but as a teacher. Because what’s become clear over the past year is that the killer app, the median American use case for products like ChatGPT, is cheating on your homework.
There’s been a lot written about this lately — a big article
dropped in New York Mag
as I was sitting down to type this newsletter, and a discord mutual had a
similarly thorough piece a couple weeks ago in the Chronicle of Higher Education
. Both pieces get into the increasing AI frustration among teachers and the increasing AI dependency among students.
There was a lot of hope for the value of AI in education (and still is, if university partnerships with tech companies are any measure). An infinitely patient digital tutor that can tackle any question (a la the Primer in Neal Stephenson’s
Diamond Age
, and probably a hundred other SF references)
sounds
like just what a strained education system needs — if it didn’t hallucinate constantly, that is. And I know teachers who use it. They’ll have students check with ChatGPT in class to get answers to discussion questions, or encourage its use in revision. Some are no doubt having AI write emails to students and paper feedback, too.
But these articles show that concern is mounting over a few factors. First, there’s a big difference between getting something explained to you, and actual learning. You might
feel
like you are learning when querying a chatbot, but those intellectual gains are often illusory.

There’s now no way to be sure that a student who turns in a good essay actually has a grasp on the material that assignment was supposed to push them toward understanding. 本文讨论了在人工智能（AI）日益普及的时代，教育领域面临的挑战，特别是学生利用AI完成作业的问题。作者借用《沙丘》中的Butlerian Jihad原则——“汝不可造出模仿人类心智的机器”——来表达对AI的反对，并指出这种反对不仅是对技术的抵制，更是一种深层次的、近乎精神层面的厌恶。文章提到，越来越多的人，包括作家和艺术家，认为与大型语言模型（LLM）的任何接触都是对创意群体的背叛。

data.title: The Difference Between Downloading and Streaming
data.author: kruemmelspalter
data.article_summary: 本文简要解释了流媒体（streaming）和下载（downloading）视频、音频等线性媒体之间的区别。尽管许多平台强调两者不同，但从技术角度看，它们基本相同。无论是流媒体还是下载，服务器都会将视频帧发送到设备，设备在播放时会暂时存储这些帧。区别在于设备如何处理这些帧：如果播放后删除，称为流媒体；如果保存为文件，则称为下载。流媒体过程中，视频播放器会预先缓存部分帧，以防止网络波动影响观看体验，因此从某种意义上说，所有流媒体都是下载。平台声称不能下载媒体，实际上依赖于用户设备在观看后删除文件的“诚信原则”。然而，用户有多种方法可以保留流媒体副本。尽管流媒体和下载在某些技术细节上（如文件顺序和压缩方式）存在差异，但从服务器角度看，它们非常相似。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： streaming与downloading的区别及其技术实现，流媒体传输协议的选择，延迟处理，网络优先级，以及版权保护技术的有效性。

不同观点：
• schoen：提出流媒体传输中使用的协议可以是不可靠的传输协议（如UDP），因为实时流不需要重传过时的数据帧，避免增加数据消耗。同时提到随着网络速度提升，TCP协议和缓冲机制解决了部分问题。对于双向通信（如电话），低延迟的UDP仍被使用。
• ryandrake：认为流媒体和下载在技术上没有本质区别，流媒体本质上也是一种下载。批评了早期客户对流媒体的误解，认为他们期望将互联网分割成不同模式是不现实的。
• Cyphase：讨论了普通用户对“下载”和“流媒体”概念的理解差异，指出在非技术用户眼中，浏览网页和下载文件的区别。
• nntwozz：从个人经验出发，强调下载在其互联网使用历史中的重要性，并列举了相关的技术工具。
• wood_spirit：指出流媒体与下载的区别更多是商业授权上的，而非技术上的。
• NoPicklez：认为流媒体和下载的区别主要在于用户意图和技术实现方式的不同，流媒体更注重实时性，下载则注重获取完整内容。
• lukax：讨论了技术上无法真正防止用户下载文件的情况，即使隐藏下载按钮也无法阻止下载行为。
• Hashex129542：详细对比了流媒体和下载的技术区别，包括数据传输方式、本地和远程处理的差异等。
• voilavilla：认为版权保护技术（如DRM）并非注定失败，未来将会有更安全的媒体传输管道，能够防止未经授权的视频截取。
• Animats：提到一些流媒体系统实际上是通过JavaScript将几秒钟的视频片段拼接成较长的视频，从而实现标准HTTPS下的流媒体播放。
• haddr：质疑是否有浏览器能够在显示内容之前存储并处理流媒体内容。
• ljsprague：认为有些观点显而易见，不必多说。
• charcircuit：质疑HDCP 2.3是否已被破解。

补充讨论：
• 关于实时流媒体和缓冲机制：schoen提到了缓冲和TCP协议的使用，使得流媒体传输更可靠，同时指出实时双向通信（如Zoom）仍然依赖UDP以降低延迟。
• 关于网络中立性和服务质量（QoS）：schoen提到过去关于流媒体优先级的争论，以及网络中立性对不同应用竞争的影响。
• 关于版权保护技术的发展：voilavilla对DRM技术的前景持乐观态度，认为未来会实现更安全的传输管道，防止未经授权的访问和拷贝。
• 关于流媒体与下载的技术细节：Hashex129542和Animats深入讨论了流媒体传输中的技术细节，包括数据分块处理、客户端拼接技术等。

争议焦点：
• 流媒体与下载的本质区别：部分讨论者认为流媒体和下载在技术上没有本质区别，而其他讨论者则认为两者在用户意图和实现方式上有显著差异。
• 版权保护技术的有效性：voilavilla认为DRM技术会不断进步并最终实现完全保护，而其他讨论者则提到历史上类似技术（如HDCP）被破解的例子。

44101072.article_content:
What’s the difference between “streaming” and “downloading” video, audio, or some other kind of linear media?
1
Many platforms make a firm distinction between streaming and downloading, implying that they’re very different. But they’re not.
They’re basically the same thing
Despite what various platforms would have you believe, there’s no significant
technical
difference between streaming and downloading.
Suppose you’re choosing whether to download or stream a video
2
.
In both cases
3
:
The server gets frames of video from a source (file, livestream, etc.)
The server sends those frames to your device
Your device stores them while it does something with them
Want to keep a copy of this animation? You don’t have to trick your computer into retaining it as it streams because
I’ve open-sourced it, and the code used to produce it
.
So what’s the difference?
The fundamental difference between streaming and downloading is what
your device
does with those frames of video:
Does it show them to you once and then throw them away? Or does it re-assemble them all back into a video file and save it into storage?
When you’re streaming on YouTube, the video player running on your computer retains a buffer of frames ahead and behind of your current position, so you can skip around easily: the
darker grey part of the timeline shows which parts of the video are stored on – that is,
downloaded
to – your computer.
Buffering
is when your streaming player gets some number of frames “ahead” of where you’re watching, to give you some protection against connection issues. If your WiFi wobbles
for a moment, the buffer protects you from the video stopping completely for a few seconds.
But for buffering to work, your computer
has
to retain bits of the video. So in a very real sense,
all
streaming
is
downloading! The buffer is the part
of the stream that’s downloaded onto your computer right now. The question is: what happens to it next?
All streaming
is
downloading
So that’s the bottom line: if your computer
deletes
the frames of video it was storing in the buffer, we call that streaming. If it
retains
them in a file, we
call that downloading.
That definition introduces a philosophical problem. Remember that Vimeo checkbox that lets a creator decide whether people can (i.e. are allowed to) download their videos?
Isn’t
that somewhat meaningless if
all streaming is downloading
.
Because if the difference between streaming and downloading is whether their device belonging to the person
watching
the video deletes the media when they’re done. And in
virtually all cases, that’s done on the honour system.
This kind of conversation happens, over the HTTP protocol,
all the time
. Probably most of the time the browser is telling the truth, but there’s no way to know for certain.
When your favourite streaming platform says that it’s only possible to stream, and not download, their media… or when they restrict “downloading” as an option to higher-cost paid plans…
they’re relying on the assumption that the user’s device can be trusted to delete the media when the user’s done watching it.
But a user who owns their own device, their own network, their own screen or speakers has many, many opportunities to not fulfil the promise of deleting media it after they’ve consumed
it: to retain a “downloaded” copy for their own enjoyment, including:
Intercepting the media as it passes through their network on the way to its destination device
Using client software that’s been configured to stream-and-save, rather than steam-and-delete, the content
Modifying “secure” software (e.g. an official app) so that it retains a saved copy rather than deleting it
Capturing the stream buffer as it’s cached in device memory or on the device’s hard disk
Outputting the resulting media to a different device, e.g. using a HDMI capture device, and saving it there
Exploiting the “analogue
4
hole”
5
:
using a camera, microphone, etc. to make a copy of what comes out of the screen/speakers
6
Okay, so I oversimplified (before you say “well, actually…”)
It’s not entirely true to say that streaming and downloading are
identical
, even with the caveat of “…from the server’s perspective”. There are three big exceptions worth
thinking about:
Exception #1: downloads can come in any order
When you stream some linear media, you
expect
the server to send the media in strict chronological order. Being able to start watching
before the whole file has
downloaded
is a big part of what makes steaming appealing, to the end-user. This means that media
intended for streaming
tends to be stored in a way that facilitates that
kind of delivery. For example:
Media designed for streaming will often be stored in linear chronological order in the file, which impacts what kinds of compression are available.
Media designed for streaming will generally use formats that put file metadata at the
start
of the file, so that it gets delivered first.
Video designed for streaming will often have frequent keyframes

data.title: Claude 4 and GitHub MCP will leak your private GitHub repositories
data.author: amrrs
data.article_summary: 文章提到，在x.com网站上，一些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会引发问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，问题通常可以通过这个方法解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub Copilot和大型语言模型（LLM）在处理私人代码和敏感信息时的安全性问题

不同观点：
• **kapitanjakc** 分享了一个具体案例，指出GitHub Copilot可能在未经授权的情况下读取私人代码库，并复制到其他项目中。他认为这可能已经持续了一段时间，并通过自己遇到的相似代码案例说明了问题。

• **losvedir** 认为，问题在于用户给LLM的访问权限过大。他指出，GitHub有细粒度的访问控制，用户应生成仅限于特定仓库的访问令牌，以减少风险。如果LLM拥有全局访问权限，那么问题更可能出在用户的安全实践上，而不是工具本身。

• **theptip** 提出了一种新的解决方案，建议使用分区子代理来隔离不同类型的任务，比如公共和私人代码库的交互。这类似于网络安全中的防火墙和安全边界概念。

• **adeon** 从安全角度出发，认为如果LLM能够从不可信的来源获取文本输入，那么这些输入可能会被用来操纵LLM生成任意文本，从而调用工具。他提到Invariant Labs提供的防护产品，并质疑AI公司是否在设计时就考虑了安全性。

• **ttoinou** 建议用户能够对每个查询精细控制LLM的访问权限，比如开启或关闭记忆功能、查询历史、连接的应用等。他认为这样可以有效减少潜在的安全风险。

• **ed** 不认为这是LLM的攻击行为，而是建议GitHub考虑引入私人草案PR机制，以便在发布前有人工审核。

• **foerster** 分享了自己遇到的情况，指出Bingbot流量请求了私人函数，这可能是Copilot或OpenAI导致的问题。

• **BeetleB** 表示只使用自己编写的MCP工具，因为审计第三方代码太费时，即使是来自“可信”组织的代码。

• **rcleveng** 开玩笑地问是否GitHub的MCP服务器代码也是由AI编写的。

• **shwouchk** 通过实验展示了LLM在不受限制的情况下可以执行的各种操作，包括提交Git代码、添加GitHub Action等。他认为这可能导致新的安全漏洞。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM和Copilot是否在未经授权的情况下访问和使用私人代码。部分用户认为这是用户安全实践不当所致，而其他人则认为工具本身应具备更多的防护措施。
• 讨论中多次提到需要更好的访问控制和防护机制，比如细粒度的权限管理和防护产品。
• 有用户对LLM的潜在滥用表示担忧，认为随着技术的发展，安全问题可能会变得更加严重。

• **kapitanjakc** 分享了一个具体案例，指出GitHub Copilot可能在未经授权的情况下读取私人代码库，并复制到其他项目中。他认为这可能已经持续了一段时间，并通过自己遇到的相似代码案例说明了问题。

• **losvedir** 认为，问题在于用户给LLM的访问权限过大。他指出，GitHub有细粒度的访问控制，用户应生成仅限于特定仓库的访问令牌，以减少风险。如果LLM拥有全局访问权限，那么问题更可能出在用户的安全实践上，而不是工具本身。

• **theptip** 提出了一种新的解决方案，建议使用分区子代理来隔离不同类型的任务，比如公共和私人代码库的交互。这类似于网络安全中的防火墙和安全边界概念。

• **adeon** 从安全角度出发，认为如果LLM能够从不可信的来源获取文本输入，那么这些输入可能会被用来操纵LLM生成任意文本，从而调用工具。他提到Invariant Labs提供的防护产品，并质疑AI公司是否在设计时就考虑了安全性。

• **ttoinou** 建议用户能够对每个查询精细控制LLM的访问权限，比如开启或关闭记忆功能、查询历史、连接的应用等。他认为这样可以有效减少潜在的安全风险。

• **ed** 不认为这是LLM的攻击行为，而是建议GitHub考虑引入私人草案PR机制，以便在发布前有人工审核。

• **foerster** 分享了自己遇到的情况，指出Bingbot流量请求了私人函数，这可能是Copilot或OpenAI导致的问题。

• **BeetleB** 表示只使用自己编写的MCP工具，因为审计第三方代码太费时，即使是来自“可信”组织的代码。

• **rcleveng** 开玩笑地问是否GitHub的MCP服务器代码也是由AI编写的。

• **shwouchk** 通过实验展示了LLM在不受限制的情况下可以执行的各种操作，包括提交Git代码、添加GitHub Action等。他认为这可能导致新的安全漏洞。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM和Copilot是否在未经授权的情况下访问和使用私人代码。部分用户认为这是用户安全实践不当所致，而其他人则认为工具本身应具备更多的防护措施。
• 讨论中多次提到需要更好的访问控制和防护机制，比如细粒度的权限管理和防护产品。
• 有用户对LLM的潜在滥用表示担忧，认为随着技术的发展，安全问题可能会变得更加严重。

data.title: Changelog: Lazy trees (faster Nix builds)
data.author: internet_points
data.article_summary: 2025年5月15日，Luc Perkins 发布了一篇关于 **Changelog** 的文章，介绍了 **Lazy Trees** 这一新功能。Lazy Trees 是 **Determinate Nix** 项目的一部分，旨在优化 Nix 构建过程。通过延迟加载和按需计算，Lazy Trees 能够显著减少内存占用并提高构建速度。这一改进对于处理大型项目和复杂依赖关系尤为重要，有助于增强 Nix 的可扩展性和性能表现。Lazy Trees 还简化了并行构建的实现，为开发者提供了更高效的构建体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nix Flakes及其相关功能（如lazy trees）的实用性、存在的问题以及社区的替代方案。

不同观点：
• **setheron的观点**：对Flakes中需要手动定义系统感到不满，认为这种做法不必要，且容易遗漏某些系统定义，导致构建失败。他希望有一种方法可以自动定义所有系统的目标，让用户自行选择需要的系统。他还表示愿意引入一些不纯的操作来解决这些问题。

• **dmvinson的观点**：认为Flakes在目前的形态下对许多人来说并不实用，尤其是在monorepos场景中。虽然Flakes不是理想的解决方案，但由于Nix拥有最大的社区，改进Flakes（如lazy trees）仍然是值得期待的。他提到，如果NixOS/Nix的维护者不喜欢Flakes/DetSys，他们应该提出一个官方的替代方案，而不能仅仅依赖于niv等小众工具。他还指出，社区有时过于追求完美，反而忽视了渐进改进的机会。

• **pxc的观点**：对lazy trees的开发进展表示兴奋，并提到自己已经通过Nix-Darwin安装了Determinate Nix进行测试。他对Eelco的工作表示赞赏，并期待lazy-trees-v2分支能尽快合并到Nix主线中。不过，他也提到Nix-Darwin模块将Nix管理方式恢复为非声明式，让他觉得有点烦人。

• **cosmic_quanta的观点**：提到在相关PR讨论中，有人指出要实现lazy trees的性能提升可能需要改变Nix语言的语义。由于自己对Nix不够熟悉，不太理解这些改变的具体影响，但认为这些技术进展仍然很有趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Flakes的实用性和其对系统定义的要求，部分用户认为这种设计不必要且容易出错。
• lazy trees功能被广泛期待，尤其是对monorepos的支持，但其合并进程和语言语义的改变可能带来不确定性。
• 社区对Nix维护者在Flakes及相关功能上的态度存在一定不满，认为需要提供一个官方的、标准的替代方案，而不是依赖于社区的小众工具。
• 用户对Determinate Nix及lazy trees等新功能的测试和反馈显示出一定的乐观态度，但也存在一些对当前实现细节的担忧。

data.title: Duolingo CEO tries to walk back AI-first comments, fails
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Duolingo的学习效果、商业模式、AI应用及其对产品质量的影响

不同观点：
• [lolinder] 认为Duolingo越来越注重通过操纵用户的注意力（如连续登录奖励等游戏化手段）来提高用户粘性，而不是帮助用户有效学习。其妻子在使用多年后因感觉学习效果下降而退出，并认为Duolingo早已偏离了其最初的教育使命。
• [eigenspace] 批评Duolingo的内容过于大众化，缺乏深度，推荐使用像Seedlang这样更注重真实语言环境的小众学习平台。Seedlang通过真实视频和语音回放帮助用户更有效地练习发音和听力。
• [amsilprotag] 指出Duolingo的用户体验问题，例如过多的弹出广告和无意义的成就展示，认为Busuu等其他平台在内容质量和用户体验上更胜一筹。
• [whyowhy3484939] 对技术在语言学习中的作用持怀疑态度，认为过度依赖技术反而导致学习效果下降，并引用多篇文章支持其观点，呼吁人们不要过度依赖技术解决非技术问题。
• [godzillabrennus] 对Duolingo用AI替代人类课程作者的做法感到失望，认为AI技术不应取代人类在教育中的核心作用，并表示将寻找其他低成本的AI工具进行语言学习。
• [in_ab] 担心AI的广泛应用会导致软件质量的下降，认为许多公司试图用AI替代人类劳动力可能会引发负面后果。
• [i80and] 表示尽管曾付费使用Duolingo，但在得知人类课程作者被AI取代后立即停止了订阅，强调付费服务应由人类提供而非AI。
• [BrandiATMuhkuh] 从学术研究和个人经验出发，认为语言学习的关键在于社会互动，AI难以替代人与人之间的互动和交流，并提出理想的语言学习应用应模仿儿童语言习得的方式。
• [hiAndrewQuinn] 介绍了自己开发的针对芬兰语学习者的开源软件，并表示通过这些工具不仅帮助了自己，还建立了专业联系，展示了小众语言学习工具的价值。
• [thenberlin] 认为如果AI可以完全替代人类教师，那么Duolingo这样的中间商平台就没有存在的必要，批评公司过度依赖AI可能会导致整个商业模式的崩溃。
• [landl0rd] 持悲观态度，认为消费者行为难以改变，尽管有用户不满Duolingo的质量下降，但大多数人仍会继续使用，公司也会继续推行其策略。
• [bayareapsycho] 从金融角度分析Duolingo的高市盈率，认为公司目前的主要目标是维持股价和吸引投资，而非提高产品质量。
• [InTheArena] 认为AI将颠覆整个软件行业，Duolingo的AI转型是行业趋势的一部分，不可避免。
• [foxfired] 通过个人经历揭示了企业追逐技术潮流的现象，指出许多技术宣传只是为了短期商业利益，而非真正改进产品。

补充讨论：
- Duolingo的游戏化设计（如连续登录奖励）被批评为过度注重用户粘性而忽视学习效果。
- 多个评论提到AI替代人类劳动力可能导致产品质量下降，并对AI在教育中的应用持怀疑态度。
- 不同用户推荐了其他语言学习平台，如Seedlang和Busuu，认为这些平台在内容和用户体验上优于Duolingo。
- 有评论从金融和商业模式角度分析Duolingo的策略，认为其主要目标是吸引投资和维持股价，而非提高教育质量。
- 争议焦点在于AI在语言学习中的应用是否能替代人类教师，以及Duolingo是否应继续依赖游戏化手段吸引用户。

data.title: Having your compile-time cake and eating it too
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust和Zig语言中的类型系统，特别是Zig中"类型即值"的特性。Zig允许在编译时对类型进行操作，例如通过函数生成条件类型如`ListIfOddLength`。然而，这种灵活性可能导致类型签名中包含过多逻辑，使得代码难以理解和推理。相比之下，Hindley-Milner类型系统通过限制类型的复杂性，提供了更人性化的体验，并支持强大的类型推断。虽然Zig的编译时运行功能有其优势，但作者认为可以结合Zig的优点与Hindley-Milner的舒适性，实现更友好的编程语言设计。作者还提出了编译时已知变量的原则，强调编译器应跟踪这些变量而不将其混入类型系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：类型的本质及其在编程语言中的表示与使用

不同观点：
• **codebje** 认为类型的本质是一个哲学问题，区分了类型是否应作为值来处理。他主张类型是规格说明（specification），而非实现（implementation），并以类型擦除（type erasure）为例说明某些语言中类型在运行时并不作为值存在。他还提出，值是程序运行时所操作的数据，而类型则属于不同的语义范畴。他认为类型到值的映射（如Hindley-Milner类型系统中的参数多态）是可行的，但从值到类型的映射则较为复杂且少见。

• **burakemir** 提到了Racket语言的多阶段编程（multistage programming）以及其在类型系统和逻辑中的表示。他指出，多阶段编程通过在运行时表示代码来实现，且已经有相关研究和实践，如Scala中的宏和多阶段编程，这些都涉及到如何在类型系统中表示程序。

• **aatd86** 对讨论的核心内容感到困惑，并尝试简化问题。他提出了几种可能性，包括高阶类型（higher kinded types）、类型检查的可判定性问题、类型是否作为一等值存在于语言的前端，以及类型是否被定义为值的集合。

补充讨论：
• **关于类型与值的哲学讨论**：codebje深入探讨了类型与值的关系，包括类型是否可以作为值、类型的类型是什么，以及这种区分是否有意义。他提到了类型系统的一致性与完备性问题，并认为依赖类型系统（dependent type system）可能是实现足够表达力且一致的类型系统的途径。

• **关于编译时与运行时的代码执行**：codebje进一步讨论了在编译时评估常量表达式的概念，并以C++中的constexpr为例，说明编译时计算的可能性。他还提到了部分求值（partial evaluation）的概念，这是一种将程序的静态部分在编译时求值的技术，可以用来优化程序执行。

• **关于多阶段编程与宏**：burakemir补充了多阶段编程的实际应用例子，如Racket的宏和Scala的相关实现。这些例子展示了如何在类型系统中表示和操作运行时的代码。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于类型是否应作为值处理，以及这种处理在实际编程语言中的可行性和意义。codebje和burakemir提供了不同的视角和实际例子，而aatd86则对讨论的核心内容提出了简化和澄清的请求。

44086935.article_content:
D
erin Eryılmaz
Having your compile-time cake and eating it too
May 24, 2025
Disclaimer
In this post, I assume:
You know a little bit about Rust.
You know a little bit about Zig.
I'll be using my own syntax to express ideas from both of these languages.
Why "types are just values" doesn't work
As programmers, we like it when our programs run well.
Type systems are there to help us with that. They track the types of values in our programs before we run them, which not only saves us from runtime crashes but enforces guidelines for writing good code.
Normally, type syntax (and logic) is distinct from the rest of a programming language. A rare exception to this rule is Zig, where types are just treated as values, and compile-time (comptime) operations on those values are allowed. That's all the type system is.
In a normal language, the
List[Int]
type is a very abstract idea. But in Zig,
List(Int)
is just a regular function call where you're inputting a
Type
and getting a
Type
back. Simple, right?
Well, if we can make a
List
function, why not a
ListIfOddLength
function that's a bit more powerful?
ListIfOddLength = (T: Type) => Type: (
if (T.to_string.length % 2 == 1) then List(T) else T
)
Okay, now let's make a generic function using it. (Square brackets introduce a type parameter.)
weird_function = [T](value: T) => ListIfOddLength(T): (
...
)
The function above takes a value with some type (
T
). If that type has an odd length, it'll return a
List(T)
, and otherwise it'll just return a
T
.
While it may not be useful,
Zig lets us express this sort of idea
. The problem is that now you're putting arbitrary logic into a type signature. To understand what type
weird_function
returns, you'll need to understand exactly how
ListIfOddLength
works. You'd have to know what
%
means and what
to_string
does.
Let's do more silly examples. Imagine that
ListIfBHash(T)
turns
T
into a string, then hashes it. The function usually returns
T
, but it'll return
List(T)
if the hash starts with a B. Or what about
ListIfAmerica
, which returns a
List(T)
if you're compiling from the United States?
With silly type-to-type functions like this, you lose the ability to reason about your program. This could be a line in your code:
y = weird_function(x)
And it could take some time to figure out the type of
y
, even if you knew what the type of
x
was. This is bad, because
type systems have to work for humans.
We see values and variables as logical things. We want to be able to express what they are in a simple way, so that we can explain them to others and understand them ourselves. Letting any operation be done on any type makes this impossible and makes a type system human-unfriendly by allowing stuff like
weird_function
.
Luckily for us, human-friendly type systems have already been invented. The most popular one is called
Hindley-Milner
(HM), and it's used by many big languages, including Swift, Rust, Scala, Haskell, OCaml, and more. (You don't need to be able to read type theory to know what HM means; just imagine the types you could write in your favorite language from that list.)
Hindley-Milner doesn't treat types as values; it treats them as abstract things that are limited to being (possibly generic) structs or enums.
By giving up that flexibility:
No more
weird_function
or
ListIfBHash
allowed.
All legal type signatures can be expressed without arbitrary logic.
Very strong type inference is supported, to the point where you almost never have to specify types.
However, Zig's comptime and type system allow for some capabilities that most HM languages can't replicate. And the ones that can (like Rust) use macros to do it, which introduces a second syntax and a whole lot of confusion.
I've seen people say Zig's features don't mix with a human-friendly type system, but I just don't think that's true. My goal in this post is to show that it's possible for a language to adopt many of them while keeping the comfort of Hindley-Milner.
Running code at compile-time
Principles:
Certain variables are known at compile-time, and the compiler should keep track of which ones are.
Most functions can be run at compile-time.
A few functions can
only
be run at compile-time.
Programmers should have to explicitly run things at compile-time. The language shouldn't do it for them.
(Keep in mind that when I call things "variables" in this blog post, I don't mean they can change. This stuff works best for a language with mostly immutable variables.)
In my opinion, the compiler should keep track of comptime-known variables, but not as part of the type system. The basic rules are simple: number/string literals are comptime-known, but function results are not.
// known
eight = 8
// not known
eight_fac = factorial(8)
An expression can be forced with
@
to make its result known at compile-time.
// known
eight_fac = @(factorial(8))
// shorter syntax
eight_fac = @factorial(8)
// another short syntax
eight_fac @= factorial(8)
These would be the same as typing
eight_fac

data.article_summary: Mutmut是一个用于Python的变异测试系统，注重易用性。它能够将发现的变异直接应用到磁盘，支持增量工作，并能识别需要执行的测试以加快变异测试速度。它具有交互式终端界面，支持并行快速执行。Mutmut要求在有fork支持的系统上运行，Windows用户需使用WSL。安装和运行简单，通过`pip install mutmut`和`mutmut run`命令即可开始。用户可以在变异结果中查看、重新测试变异，并将变异应用到代码中。配置文件`setup.cfg`或`pyproject.toml`中可设置变异路径、测试目录等选项。系统支持Unix文件名模式匹配、限制堆栈深度以加快测试速度，并允许排除特定文件或代码行的变异。变异示例包括改变整数文字和比较运算符等。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• MichaelNolan认为变异测试是一个很好的想法，但对具体库不熟悉，仅在Java项目中使用过PiTest。他指出，变异测试在共享库代码中非常有用，能增强对代码正确性的信心。
