data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用AI生成客户推荐视频的合法性、AI视频生成服务的真实性及其价格合理性

不同观点：
• [_jayhack_] 认为使用AI生成的视频作为客户推荐是违法的，表达了对这种做法的道德和法律质疑。
• [harmmonica] 对提交该项目的用户（pscsbs）是否与公司有关联提出质疑，并讨论了如果AI视频生成真的只需几分钟，那么高价格是否合理的问题。他推测，如果真能这么快生成，那么公司的毛利率会非常高，除非研发成本极高。他还建议更详细地说明"几分钟"的具体含义以及后续的人工参与程度。
• [growthwtf] 则明确表示，行业内凡是超过10分钟制作时间和收费高于个位数美元的服务，通常都涉及大量人工，而不是真正的AI。他暗示，那些号称使用AI的服务可能在宣传上存在夸大。

补充讨论：
• [t_schmidt] 对项目方是否为spacial dot io提出疑问，指出该公司网站上显示的是结构和机电（MEP）服务，而非AI视频生成服务，可能存在误认公司的问题。

争议焦点：
1. 使用AI生成客户推荐视频的合法性和道德性。
2. AI视频生成服务的真实性及其价格合理性。
3. 项目方与提交项目方的身份关联以及实际服务内容的确认。

data.title: Most leading chatbots routinely exaggerate science findings
data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: 一项由乌得勒支大学和西安大略大学等机构进行的研究发现，高达73%的领先聊天机器人（如ChatGPT、DeepSeek、Claude等）在总结科学论文时会产生不准确的结论。研究分析了近5000份机器人总结，发现其中六成模型经常夸大原始文本中的主张，特别是将谨慎的过去时表述改为更为广泛的现在时，例如将“该治疗在这项研究中有效”变为“该治疗有效”，从而可能误导读者。更令人担忧的是，当用户要求避免不准确信息时，这些模型反而更频繁地产生夸大结论。研究建议使用如Claude等表现较好的模型，并通过降低聊天机器人的“温度”参数来减少风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）产生夸张输出的问题及其与学术媒体、新闻报道中夸张或过度自信声明的关系

不同观点：
• **[rekenaut的观点]**：LLM产生夸张输出可能与学术媒体或新闻报道中对研究结果的夸张描述有关。模型从这些报道中学习，因此容易模仿这种吸引注意力的风格，即使在直接使用研究资料时也是如此。

• **[GiorgioG的观点]**：对LLM的实际表现感到失望，特别是在处理复杂任务时。他指出，LLM经常偏离预期轨道，给出未经授权的输出，并且在纠正后的内容上仍会犯错。他认为这些工具尚未成熟，不值得投入的大量资金。

• **[delichon的观点]**：LLM本质上是抽象机器，依赖于高维空间中的相邻数据进行输出。LLM依赖统计模型作为真理来源，而要达到“公正见证者”式的AI推理能力，需要超越统计的方法，可能导致复杂的结果。

• **[proc0的观点]**：LLM并不具备真正的推理能力，其错误通常是随机且无意义的。当前的技术进展似乎未能解决这一问题，尤其是在图像和视频生成之外的领域。

• **[bethekidyouwant的观点]**：夸大科学发现的现象并非LLM独有，而是普遍存在于领先的聊天机器人中。

• **[Aurornis的观点]**：在线论坛中，LLM被广泛用于获取医疗建议，特别是在难以获得医生答案的情况下。然而，这导致了大量复制粘贴的LLM回答，甚至引发错误信息的传播，取代了过去由替代医学和补充剂占据的市场。

• **[Mistletoe的观点]**：LLM被训练的数据包括了点击诱饵文章和大学的新闻发布，这些通常会错误解读和夸大科学的重要性。

• **[ekianjo的观点]**：LLM在主流媒体上训练，学习了糟糕的科学报道方式，因此产生夸张输出是意料之中的。

• **[gustavus的观点]**：通过对4,900份摘要的分析，发现十个模型中有六个会系统性地夸大原始文本中的声明，这与科学记者的错误相似。

• **[more_corn的观点]**：主流新闻媒体经常夸大科学发现，这也是一个普遍现象。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于LLM是否能够实现真正的推理能力，以及它们在处理复杂任务和科学信息时的可靠性。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，LLM夸大信息的问题并非孤立现象，而是与更广泛的媒体和市场环境有关。
• 讨论中还提到，LLM在医疗等敏感领域的使用可能会导致错误信息的传播，造成实际生活中的问题。

44102378.article_content:
Most leading chatbots routinely exaggerate science findings
ChatGPT is often asked for summaries, but how accurate are these really?
1 May 2025
It seems so convenient: when you are short of time, asking ChatGPT or another chatbot to summarise a scientific paper to quickly get a gist of it. But in up to 73 per cent of the cases, these large language models (LLMs) produce inaccurate conclusions, a new study by
Uwe Peters
(Utrecht University) and
Benjamin Chin-Yee
(Western University and University of Cambridge) finds.
Almost 5,000 LLM-generated summaries analysed
The researchers tested ten of the most prominent LLMs, including ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude, and LLaMA. “We entered abstracts and articles from top science journals, such as
Nature
,
Science
, and
The Lancet
,” says Peters, “and asked the models to summarise them. Our key question: how accurate are the summaries that the models generate?”
Which chatbots did Peters and Chin-Yee test?
Peters and Chin-Yee tested ten leading older and very recent chatbots:
GPT-3.5 Turbo
GPT-4 Turbo
LLaMA 2 70B
Claude 2
ChatGPT-4o
ChatGPT-4.5
LLaMA 3.3 70B
Claude 3.5 Sonnet
Claude 3.7 Sonnet
DeepSeek
Summaries by models (1), (4), (8), and (9) didn’t significantly differ in the kind of generalisations they contained from the original text. “So basically,” Peters concludes, “Claude, in different versions, did really well.”
“Over a year, we collected 4,900 summaries. When we analysed them, we found that six of ten models systematically exaggerated claims they found in the original texts. Often the differences were subtle. But nuances can be of great importance in making sense of scientific findings.”
For instance, LLMs often changed cautious, past-tense claims into more sweeping, present-tense versions: ‘The treatment was effective in this study’ became ‘The treatment is effective’. “Changes like this can mislead readers,” Chin-Yee warns. “They can give the impression that the results are more widely applicable than they really are.”
When asked for more accuracy, the chatbots exaggerated even more often.
The researchers also directly compared human-written with LLM-generated summaries of the same texts. Chatbots were nearly five times more likely to produce broad generalisations than their human counterparts.
Accuracy prompts backfired
Peters and Chin-Yee did try to get the LLMs to generate accurate summaries. They, for instance, specifically asked the chatbots to avoid inaccuracies. “But strikingly, the models then produced exaggerated conclusions even
more
often”, Peters says. “They were nearly twice as likely to produce overgeneralised conclusions.”
“This effect is concerning. Students, researchers, and policymakers may assume that if they ask ChatGPT to avoid inaccuracies, they will get a more reliable summary. Our findings suggest the exact opposite.”
Newer AI models, like ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek, performed even worse.
Why are these exaggerations happening?
“LLMs may inherit the tendency to make broader claims from the texts they are trained with,” Chin-Yee explains. He refers to
findings in previous studies
. “Human experts also tend to draw more general conclusions, from Western samples to all people, for example.”
“But lots of the original articles didn’t contain
problematic
generalisations, but the summaries then suddenly did,” Peters adds. “Worse still, overall, newer AI models, like ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek, performed worse than older ones.”
Another reason for LLMs’ generalisation bias might lie in people’s interaction with the chatbots. “In their interactions with LLMs, human users that are involved in the models’ fine-tuning may prefer LLM responses that sound helpful and widely applicable. In this way, the models might learn to favour such answers – even at the expense of accuracy.”
There is a real risk that AI-generated science summaries could spread misinformation.
Reducing the risks
“If we want AI to support science literacy rather than undermine it, we need more vigilance and testing of LLMs in science communication contexts,” Peters stresses. “These tools are already being widely used for science summarisation, so their outputs can shape public science understanding – accurately or misleadingly. Without proper oversight, there is a real risk that AI-generated science summaries could spread misinformation, or present uncertain science as settled fact.”
If you still wish to use a chatbot to summarise a text, Peters and Chin-Yee recommend using LLMs such as Claude, which had the highest generalisation accuracy. It may also help to use prompts that enforce indirect, past-tense reporting, and, if you are a programmer, to set chatbots to lower ‘temperature’ (the parameter fixing a chatbot’s ‘creativity’).
About Uwe Peters and Benjamin Chin-Yee
Dr Uwe Peters holds an MSc in Neuroscience and Psychology of Mental Health, and a PhD in Philosophy both from King’s College London, United Kingdom. He is currently assistant professor at Utrecht University, where he is work

data.title: Understanding Memory Management, Part 6: Basic Garbage Collection
data.author: ekr____
data.article_summary: 本文是关于内存管理的系列文章的第六部分，聚焦于基本的垃圾回收机制。作者首先回顾了之前文章中对C、C++和Rust内存管理的介绍，指出即便C++的RAII和Rust简化了内存管理，程序员仍需关注内存使用。文章引出垃圾回收（Garbage Collection, GC）的概念，即由系统自动管理内存分配和释放，无需程序员手动操作。通过对比C和JavaScript代码示例，作者说明了在支持垃圾回收的语言中，内存管理对程序员是透明的，系统自动处理内存分配和回收。为了更好地解释垃圾回收的原理，作者设计了一种名为Memo的小型语言，用于展示不同垃圾回收策略的效果，而不受复杂语言机制的干扰。

44100216.article_content:
Understanding Memory Management, Part 6: Basic Garbage Collection
Posted by
ekr
on 26 May 2025
This is the sixth post in my multipart series on memory
management. You will probably want to go back and read Part
I
, which covers C, parts
II
and
III
, which cover C++, and parts
IV
and
V
which cover Rust.
C++ RAII and Rust
do a lot to simplify memory management but still
force you to constantly think about how you are using memory (this is
even more true with Rust). It's natural to ask why we have to do all
this work and why the computer can't just figure things out. The
answer is that it can—at a cost—which brings us to the
other major approach to handling memory: automatic memory
management/aka garbage collection.
[1]
In this post, I want to introduce the basic ideas behind
garbage collection and describe the main algorithms which
provide the basis for modern GC systems.
What behavior do we want?
#
In C and C++, the programmer is responsible for two major memory
management tasks:
Allocating new memory on the heap when it's needed
Returning unused memory back to the heap so it can be re-allocated
later.
In C, these operations are both completely manual using
malloc()
and
free()
C++ provides manual memory management with
new
and
delete
, but also provides various mechanisms to automatically
allocate and deallocate memory, such as container classes, RAII and smart pointers;
the programmer is still frequently responsible for explicitly
allocating objects and has to understand their lifetimes.
Similarly, Rust requires you to explicitly manage memory,
but protects you from errors when you fail to do so.
In a wide variety of languages, ranging from Go to JavaScript, the
system handles all of these operations automatically completely. The
programmer just creates variables and objects and the language takes
care of allocating memory as required and de-allocates the memory at
an appropriate time. To see this in action, consider the following
trivial C function and its JavaScript equivalent:
C
#
void
foo
(
)
{
int
a
=
1
;
int
b
[
2
]
=
{
1
}
;
size_t
b_len
=
1
;
b
[
b_len
++
]
=
2
;
}
JS
#
function
foo
(
)
{
let
a
=
1
let
b
=
[
1
]
b
.
push
(
2
)
}
Both versions of this code to the same thing. First, they create two
variables.
a
: An integer set to one
b
: A list consisting of the single integer 1
We then push another element onto
b
to make the list
[1, 2]
.
The first line of the function is basically the same in both languages.
Take a look at the second line, however, where we create
b
. This
C code actually makes two memory-related decisions:
It puts the memory on the stack (because we didn't call
malloc()
)
It allocates a fixed-size array of size 2.
Note that even though we only add one value (
1
) to
b
, the array is
still of size 2. This is why we need a separate length field
b_len
to keep track of how many elements are actually in
b
. The syntax
{1}
tells C to initialize the array with
1
and then as many zeros
as are required to fill the rest of the array. Except for the
initialization, this should all be pretty familiar from part
I
.
Now compare the corresponding JS code, which looks fairly
similar, but that's just because JS imitates C syntax. Just
like in C, we make a local variable
b
that can hold
a list of things, but we never explicitly tell JS whether it
should be on the stack or the heap or how big it should be.
So, what are the answers to those questions? Who knows? Who cares?
None of your business! The JS engine will do whatever it thinks best,
and may not even do the same thing every time. Specifically:
The JS engine will automatically grow
b
whenever you
add new elements. In this respect it's like the
C++
vector
container.
Local variables can be stored on either the stack or the
heap. In fact, they can be stored in one place and then
moved to the other when conditions change; it's totally
up to the JS engine.
Whatever the JS engine does, it's essentially transparent to
the programmer, who just writes code and lets the language
worry about it. The same thing applies to many other languages
like JS, Python, Lisp, etc.
In these languages, just as you don't have to worry about when you are
allocating memory, you also don't have to worry about de-allocating
it; the language automatically detects when you aren't using memory
and de-allocates it, in a process called "garbage collection" (commonly,
GC).
You just write code!
[2]

#
In this post, we'll be taking a slightly different approach
than with previous posts. Because the internals of garbage
collection are (mostly) invisible and real-world garbage
collectors are very complicated, working with a real language
isn't that useful for explanatory purposes. Instead,
I've designed and implemented a tiny language called
Memo
(for "memory demo") that lets us look at the
impact of various garbage collection approaches without
being distracted byu a lot of language mechanics.

conditionals or l

Three Days?
Several users are currently reporting
Community Notes on X
have disappeared from their timelines. This is not by itself unusual, sometimes notes that are voted "helpful" by Community Notes users later get downvoted into "not helpful" status. But right now it appears even notes that have reached "helpful" status in Community Note's user interface are not being displayed on the public version of the X posts they are attached to.
Take this
post for example
(archived
here
):
In the list of posts with notes that are "Rated helpful" in the interface used by Community Notes contributors, this is currently the top one:
But instead of a list of the helpful notes that would normally appear under it there is just a link to "See all notes on this post".
That link goes here
, if you are a Community Notes contributor you can see it. That page clearly shows there is at least one note voted helpful:
However the note does not show up on the public facing version of the post as of this writing.
A sampling of the other posts on the "Rated helpful" tab shows the same pattern: no notes visible on the public posts but "helpful" notes being available behind the "See all notes on this post" link.
Community Notes users who click the three dots in the top right corner of a post and click the "Write a Community Note" button still get to see existing Community Notes on a post, indicating the notes are still there, they are just not being displayed publicly. It appears proposed notes also don't show up on public posts for Community Notes users at the moment, making it much harder for notes to acquire enough votes to allow the Community Notes algorithm to run its consensus algorithm.
Several users apparently reported seeing the same issue and complained about missing Community Notes, some as early as Saturday, May 24, 2025, three days ago:

主要讨论点：发射探空仪的个人经历和环境挑战

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：cozzyd分享了自己在格陵兰 summit 站发射探空仪的亲身经历，强调了在恶劣天气条件下（30节的风）操作的困难。具体描述了探空仪在强风中不断拍打其头部的情况，最终成功释放并快速升空。这个观点主要突出了在极端环境下工作的挑战性和独特的个人体验。

• 第二种观点：cozzyd还提到自己在南极点参与了探空仪的发射，但并非由其本人亲手释放。这里表达了一种部分参与的经历，虽然没有亲自完成关键动作，但仍然是对探空仪发射过程的贡献和体验。

补充讨论：
- 操作环境：评论中提到的格陵兰和南极点都是极端天气环境，强调了在这些地方工作所需的特殊技能和应对能力。
- 个人参与度：cozzyd在两次发射中的角色略有不同，一次是主要执行者，另一次是辅助角色，显示了在科学研究活动中多样化的参与方式。
- 具体细节：提供了风速和探空仪运动的具体细节，增强了对发射过程的生动描述，使读者更容易理解现场情况。

data.title: FromSoft's singular mech game Chromehounds is back online
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了FromSoftware的一款被低估的机甲游戏《Chromehounds》正在被粉丝社区复活。该游戏最初于2010年因服务器关闭而无法在线游玩，但最近在一些热心粉丝和模组制作者的努力下，重新实现了6v6的多人对战。游戏特色在于团队协作、自定义机甲和独特的非对称角色，需要玩家通过语音交流来协调战术，特别是在争夺通讯塔和领土战争中。尽管《Chromehounds》当年并未大热，但其忠实粉丝一直致力于让它重现生机。模组制作者ImagineBeingAtComputers通过一系列技术探索，最终成功恢复了游戏的在线功能，让这款老游戏再次焕发活力。文章还提到，类似《Phasmophobia》和《Lethal Company》这样的游戏证明，只要有足够吸引力，玩家仍愿意参与公共语音交流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对不同机甲游戏的评价与期待，包括对游戏机制、网络代码公平性、历史地位以及重制的可能性等方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• [aetherspawn] 认为《MechWarrior Online》在网络代码的公平性上表现出色，尤其是解决了全球玩家ping差异的问题，使得游戏体验更加公平。他提到机甲有多个独立受击区，细微的网络差异可能会导致游戏不公平，但《MechWarrior Online》最终解决了这个问题。

• [gimmeThaBeet] 表达了对《Chromehounds》的怀旧情感，特别提到了游戏中的三方冲突和文明设计（如NATO型、东方集团和中东文明）具有超前性。他还提到FromSoftware在机甲游戏领域的悠久历史，认为《Chromehounds》并非其唯一的出色作品。

• [typesarecool] 表达了对《Chromehounds》重制的期待，提到自己过去只在单人模式中体验过该游戏，并希望能在现代主机平台上看到续作或重制版。

• [pawanjswal] 对《Chromehounds》的讨论表示感慨，称其为“狂野而真诚的复活”，似乎对该游戏的情感触动表示认同。

• [tra3] 提到了自己过去玩《War Robots》的经历，并暗指该游戏存在“付费取胜”的机制，暗示对这种模式的不满。

• [ninetyninenine] 认为《Virtual On》是难以被复制的经典机甲游戏，特别提到其独特的火箭侧冲和闪避机制，连《Armored Core》也无法模仿这种效果。

• [absurdo] 以幽默方式提到《Chromehounds》是《Chromelords》的前作，似乎在调侃两款游戏之间的关联或相似性。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点之一是不同机甲游戏的独特机制和难以复制的经典元素，例如《Virtual On》的闪避机制。
- 玩家对《Chromehounds》的情感和对重制的期待是另一个重要讨论点，部分玩家希望能够在现代平台上看到该游戏的续作或重制版。
- 网络代码的公平性在多人在线游戏中被视为一个重要问题，特别是对于具有复杂受击区和精准射击机制的游戏。

44102988.article_content:
[Chromehounds lobby]
Me: [chanting] mechs, mechs-
Other pilots: Mechs, MECHS
Mechanic: [pounding her toolbox] MECHS, MECHS, MECHS!
Hello! Apologies for the late issue, but this story came together last minute, on account of capital-L Life, and also because the subject is developing
fast
. Hopefully it's worth the wait! I've got an exclusive interview for you on a shit-hot community project to resurrect a FromSoftware game that was criminally underappreciated in its day. I mean, that's practically all FromSoftware games, but this one was just born in the wrong time and place — I think it would be a substantial hit on Steam in the year 2025.
But I'm getting ahead of myself, while also being behind. So let's jump right into it! It's big stompy robot time.
The Big One
1. Bringing back the FromSoftware mech game that was a decade ahead of its time
On Wednesday, Resetera member wwm0nkey
posted a thread
I've been waiting to see for years:
"Fans are working to bring From Software's ChromeHounds back online."
But the news is actually even better than that: they've already succeeded. For the first time since Sega shut down the servers in 2010, FromSoftware's most inspired mech game is playable again, with a small group of diehard fans currently battling it out in up to 6v6 multiplayer matches.
The tl;dr on Chromehounds: it's a team-based, PvP mech game with customizable machines and unique asymmetrical roles that demanded true collaboration to succeed. Heavy mechs too slow to maneuver around the battlefield had to sit on the backlines, firing off artillery shots at the direction of the frontline troops. Commanders held squads together, dishing out information and orders. Capturing communication towers was the only way to keep comms open, and their limited range meant pushing into enemy territory likely meant intense, high risk radio silence. Battles fed into a meta-level conflict between warring nations, with enough wins for one side eventually resulting in conquest of a capital city and a reset of the whole war. This video from YouTube channel Save Data breaks it all down in more detail, and what made it so unique at the time — which honestly still applies today.
Chromehounds was, of course, never big, but the players who loved it
really
loved it. What I found most fascinating about it (from a distance, because it never made it off my "I should try that sometime" list in the Xbox 360 era) was how battles hinged on the implementation of voice chat, which was still novel and exciting on consoles then. Everyone was guaranteed to have that dinky 360 headset, but few games treated communication as a malleable mechanic. Empowering certain players to distribute information and drawing stark boundaries between where you could and couldn't reach your team flooded the tactical playspace with so many possibilities even before you got to customizing mechs or outshooting your enemies.
There was a beautiful but brief window after the launch of the Xbox 360 in late 2005 when developers were experimenting with these sorts of voice chat ideas, and of course FromSoftware would come up with a fascinating (and underappreciated) game built around it. Two years after Chromehounds came out, Microsoft effectively made games like it extinct by releasing Party Chat, which allowed everyone to skip out on public chat and talk only with their friends.
While the situation is much the same now, with most of us sequestered in private Discords whenever we play, I think the success of games like Phasmophobia and Lethal Company — and the audience for games on PC now being bigger and more varied than ever — shows that people
will
hop in public voice for a compelling enough idea.
Likewise, the diehards who truly love Chromehounds will, to this day, jump through the hackiest set of hoops imaginable for a chance to experience its magic once again.
"I'm glad people trusted me, because I don't know if I would've quite trusted me up to that point. 'Hey, this 15-year-old game is running; all you have to do is run this EXE that Windows says is bad," jokes ImagineBeingAtComputers, the modder behind Chromehounds' comeback.
ImagineBeingAtComputers set up a Discord server called OpenCOMBAS in 2023 after setting out to try to revive the game and eventually finding a developer debug build. "What this gets us isn't quite clear yet, but it definitely gets us closer," he wrote in the server's announcement channel. Then a year went by. The debug build of the game granted him access to lots of useful information about how Chromehounds worked, but it wasn't the silver bullet it may sound like. In May 2024 he posted in the Discord that he was at an impassable dead end, with no idea how to revive the game's online multiplayer.
In just the last few days, everything's changed. And it's changed so fast that the announcement channel hasn't even yet been updated with the good news. But OpenCOMBAS members trusting enough to download ch_server.exe have found themselves in live ma

data.title: Ask HN: What projects do you donate to?
data.author: xeonmc
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目和数字基础设施的捐赠行为及选择

不同观点：
• **支持捐赠特定开源项目和数字平台**：
  - **neom** 推荐阅读 Nadia Asparouhova 的报告《Roads and Bridges: The Unseen Labor Behind Our Digital Infrastructure》，强调支持开源社区以外的改变。
  - **vallassy** 提到自己捐赠给诸如 Octoprint、Internet Archive 等免费提供服务的平台。
  - **slyall** 每年都会公开自己的捐赠项目，包括 Syncthing、Python、Let's Encrypt 等，但因支付方式问题，停止了对一些组织的捐赠。
  - **cperciva** 支持 FreeBSD 基金会和其他开源项目。
  - **elevaet** 支持 LibreOffice、Internet Archive、Wikipedia 和 Bandcamp，认为通过 Bandcamp 支持独立艺术家具有重要意义。
  - **Arubis** 捐赠给 EFF、ACLU、Mastodon 实例和 magit.vc 等技术相关项目。
  - **WillAdams** 通过 Microsoft Rewards 点数捐赠给 Wikipedia，并支持个人开发者。
  - **ajdude** 捐赠给 Internet Archive、Let's Encrypt、Ironclad 和 Alire，因为这些项目对其工作有直接帮助。
  - **wonger_** 支持日常使用的工具 Min 浏览器和 fman。

• **捐赠选择基于个人背景和需求**：
  - **raydenvm** 来自乌克兰，捐赠给 United24 和 Come Back Alive Foundation，认为这些捐赠对阻止战争有帮助。

• **质疑捐赠的必要性和平台状况**：
  - **zabzonk** 认为互联网和网站并没有如一些人所说的那样正在消亡，质疑在网络上进行捐赠行为的必要性，并反对在讨论中进行“道德表演”。

• **对捐赠行为的信任问题**：
  - **Elaris** 表示自己很少在互联网上捐赠，因为很难验证许多项目的真实性，倾向于亲自了解情况后再做决定，认为捐赠应该针对真实和有形的事物。

补充讨论：
- **支付方式的影响**：一些捐赠者如 **slyall** 提到支付方式（如 Paypal）对捐赠选择的影响，尤其在亚太地区。
- **个人项目支持**：如 **WillAdams** 支持个人开发者，通过实际使用体验决定捐赠。
- **地区性捐赠**：如 **raydenvm** 基于个人背景支持与战争相关的基金，反映出地区冲突对个人捐赠选择的影响。

  - **Elaris** 表示自己很少在互联网上捐赠，因为很难验证许多项目的真实性，倾向于亲自了解情况后再做决定，认为捐赠应该针对真实和有形的事物。

补充讨论：
- **支付方式的影响**：一些捐赠者如 **slyall** 提到支付方式（如 Paypal）对捐赠选择的影响，尤其在亚太地区。
- **个人项目支持**：如 **WillAdams** 支持个人开发者，通过实际使用体验决定捐赠。
- **地区性捐赠**：如 **raydenvm** 基于个人背景支持与战争相关的基金，反映出地区冲突对个人捐赠选择的影响。

data.title: Yes-rs: A fast, memory-safe rewrite of the classic Unix yes command
data.author: ericdiao
data.article_summary: "yes-rs" 是一个用 Rust 重写的 Unix 经典命令 `yes`，具有更高的内存安全性和性能。原版的 `yes` 命令用 C 编写，存在内存安全问题和性能局限。而 "yes-rs" 具有以下特点：内存安全、速度极快、支持零成本抽象、可实现无畏并发，并完全使用 Rust 编写，易于通过 Cargo 安装和管理。用户可以通过 `cargo install yes-rs` 安装，并用其输出 "y" 或其他自定义字符串。该项目旨在展示 Rust 在系统编程中的优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Rust项目"yes-rs"的代码规模、复杂性、技术方向、以及一些幽默评论的讨论。

不同观点：
• **alberth**认为该项目的代码量是GNU版本的26倍，管理和维护成本更高，可能还会引入新的工具链，对成本效益的分析将很有趣。
• **selcuka**通过一系列幽默的错误处理示例，暗示Rust在错误处理上比C++更具优势，但也提到了一些看似不可能发生的错误。
• **mjmas**提到该项目将在6个月后被放弃，并推荐了几个替代项目，这些项目使用了不同的架构和依赖。
• **tptacek**以讽刺口吻建议将项目拆分为12个不同的crate，暗示项目可能过度复杂化。
• **kidmin**提到一个用Java编写的企业级项目，暗示当前Rust项目的复杂性和必要性可能被夸大。
• **layer8**指出代码中缺少本地化处理，并以乌兹别克语的“no”为例，认为Rust的类型系统未捕捉到这种潜在错误。
• **adastra22**批评了一些人在未阅读源代码前就发表评论。
• **thadt**对项目的量子抵抗安全声明表示怀疑，指出代码中未见任何后量子算法，并提到一些未使用的优化标志，暗示这些可能是未来解决问题的路线图。
• **sethops1**建议增加原生Kubernetes集成和Helm chart支持，以提升项目的实用性。
• **k3vinw**赞赏项目的幽默和奉献精神，提到项目问题也得到了同等重视。
• **juped**以幽默方式提到隐藏不安全的代码，并表示对量子相关的幽默不太理解。
• **csmantle**认为该项目展示了Rust不该成为的样子，暗示其过度复杂和不必要的设计。
• **pawanjswal**表示非常喜欢项目的“Rust能量”，赞赏其夸张的风格。
• **otikik**幽默地表示期待项目2.0版加入AI功能。
• **rurban**认为这是一个对“疯狂”人群的实用玩笑。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于项目的复杂性和实用性。一些评论者认为项目过度复杂，而另一些评论者则欣赏其幽默和夸张的风格。
• 对项目的本地化和错误处理也存在一定讨论，特别是对Rust类型系统未能捕捉潜在错误的批评。
• 量子抵抗安全声明和未来路线图的未实现部分也引发了质疑。

data.title: Show HN: I made a running app that turns your runs to a virtual garden
data.author: Utkarshn101
data.article_summary: 《Grow a Running Habit That Sticks》介绍了一款名为Run&Grow的应用程序，帮助用户养成持久的跑步习惯。该应用通过可视化的“数字花园”展示跑步进展，用户完成跑步后可获得植物作为奖励，随着持续跑步，花园逐渐扩展。应用提供温和的提醒和成就系统，鼓励自我竞争而非与他人比较，避免传统跑步应用中的压力和无趣感。用户通过设定目标、追踪跑步、收集植物来培养习惯，最终建立长期的跑步routine。应用免费下载，提供高级功能解锁选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[围绕一款新应用的各种功能和设计建议，以及对潜在问题的讨论]

不同观点：
• [Raudius] 认为应用没有提供免费试用是一种不良的商业模式（dark pattern）。他希望在决定是否需要更多高级功能前，能够先试用免费版本以了解基础功能。

• [pgt] 对应用的预期功能有不同的理解，原本期待应用能在虚拟地图上模拟种植和浇灌的过程，类似于Strava的运动路线可视化功能。

• [lispisok] 对应用的核心概念表示赞赏，提到自己曾有将好习惯游戏化的想法，并询问开发者关于使用Capacitor（一个应用开发工具）的经验。

• [coderag] 关注应用的社交功能，建议增加Strava的集成，以便利用其现有的社交网络。

• [deadbabe] 认为该应用可以扩展到其他领域，比如用于可视化GitHub的提交记录，以此增强其适用范围。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点集中在应用的免费试用问题上，[Raudius] 认为缺乏免费试用是一种不透明的策略，可能影响用户的信任和使用意愿。

• 其他用户如 [pgt]、[coderag] 和 [deadbabe] 则更多是在讨论应用的功能扩展和与其他平台的集成可能性，显示出对应用未来发展的兴趣和期望。

• [lispisok] 关注开发技术方面，特别是对Capacitor的使用经验感兴趣，这表明部分讨论也涉及到开发者社区内部的技术交流。

data.author: kaycebasques
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何创建和管理超文本知识库，以及相关工具的可持续性和易用性。

不同观点：
• [coderatlarge] 指出，许多科学家、学生和爱好者希望创建自己的基于标签的超文本知识库，但历史上所需的工具组合非常复杂，尤其是Gerby软件及其依赖项已难以在现代环境中构建，这引发了对其长久性的质疑。

• [pastage] 认为，Web在其发展历程中经历了三次重大冲击：弹出式广告、SEO内容农场和当前的LLM生成内容泛滥。尽管不热衷于使用TeX进行写作，但认为像Gerby这样的项目通过专注于发布知识图谱的工具改进是有价值的。同时，强调所见即所得（wysiwyg）的工具因其易用性会始终占据优势。

补充讨论：
• [pastage] 提到了对TeX在写作方面的保留意见，认为复杂的Markdown类似于TeX，但强调在布局方面TeX仍然是合适的选择。
• [pastage] 进一步指出，当前LLM生成内容的泛滥对Web的原始生态构成了威胁，这成为改进知识库工具的一个动机。
• 争议的焦点在于工具的复杂性与易用性之间的平衡。一方面是像Gerby这样功能强大但依赖复杂的工具，另一方面是所见即所得的工具因其用户友好性更有可能被广泛采用。

总结来看，讨论围绕着创建和管理超文本知识库的工具复杂性、可持续性和用户体验展开，涉及到历史工具的局限性与现代需求之间的矛盾。

总结来看，讨论围绕着创建和管理超文本知识库的工具复杂性、可持续性和用户体验展开，涉及到历史工具的局限性与现代需求之间的矛盾。

Get affordable and hassle-free WordPress hosting plans with Cloudways —
start your free trial today
.
Ever heard of favicons made with SVG? If you are a regular reader of CSS-Tricks, you probably have. But does your website actually use one?
The task is more non-trivial than you might think. As we will see in this article, creating a useful SVG favicon involves editing an SVG file manually, which is something many of us try to avoid or are uncomfortable doing. Plus, we are talking about a
favicon
. We can spend a few hours playing with a hot new CSS framework. But a favicon? It sometimes feels too small to be worth our time.
This article is about creating an SVG favicon
for real
. If you’re in front of your laptop, get the vector file of a logo ready. By the end of your (active!) reading, your SVG favicon will be ready to shine.
Why an SVG favicon at all?
We are here for the “how” but it’s worth reflecting: what is an SVG favicon even good for? We already have other file types that handle this, right?
SVG is a vector format. As such, it has valuable features over raster formats, including those typically used for favicons, like PNG. SVGs scale and are often more compact than its binary cousins because, well, they’re just code!
Everything is drawn in numbers and letters!
That’s good news, but how does this help our favicon? Desktop favicons are small,
at most 64×64
. And you can ship your
icons in several resolutions
. Scaling is a feature we don’t really need here.
File size is another source of disappointment. While SVG has a clear edge over a high resolution PNG file, the tables turn in low resolution. It is common for a 48×48 PNG favicon to result in a smaller file size than its SVG equivalent.
Yet, we have a good reason to pay attention to SVG favicon:
dark mode support
.
Dark mode
has received a lot of attention recently. You may even have implemented dark mode for your own websites. What does that mean for favicon? It means the ability to show different icons based on the brightness of the browser tab’s background.
We are going to prepare such an icon.
How to create an SVG favicon (in theory)
Getting dark mode support for an SVG favicon relies on a CSS trick (10 points to Gryffindor), namely that we can drop a
<style>
tag right inside SVG, and use a media query to detect the user’s current theme preference. Something like this:
<svg>
<style>
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
// Your dark styles here
}
</style>
<!-- more stuff -->
</svg>
With this pattern, your light/dark favicon is only limited by your imagination. For example,
change the color of all lines
:
<svg>
<style>
path { fill: black; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
path { fill: white; }
}
</style>
<!-- more stuff -->
</svg>
Now is the time to actually write these styles. This is when the troubles begin.
SVGs are images, and the logo we are using to build our favicon was probably created with a tool like Adobe Illustrator or InkScape. Why not use the same tool again? That’s because apps like these haven’t really integrated CSS and media queries into their products. It’s not that they can’t handle them, but you have to forget the mouse-only experience they promise. You are going to use the keyboard and type code.
Which leads us to a second option: write the CSS by hand. After all, this is the way to go with front-end development. Why should it be different here? Unfortunately, SVG is often hard to read. Sure, this is an XML dialect, which is (almost) like HTML. But SVG images are cluttered with long
path
declarations and other markup we often don’t see in our day-to-day work. For example, the Raspberry Pi logo is more than 8KB of raw data. This make manual editing more tedious than it sounds.
That is a lot of code.
How to create an SVG favicon (in practice)
To understand how we can deal with an SVG favicon quickly and easily, we first need to define what we want to achieve.
The technique we covered above calls for creativity: replace a color, invert them all (which we’ll get to), change a shape… But the setup for a favicon is not the right time for this. A favicon should almost always be the website’s logo. Its appearance? Aesthetic? The message it conveys? All these questions have been answered already. Preparing the favicon should be fine-tuning the logo so it fits the small space allocated in browser tabs.
Often, the logo is perfect as-is and its favicon counterpart is a scaled down version of it. Sometimes, we need to add margin to make it square. What motivates a dark icon, then?
Contrast.
Many logos are designed for light backgrounds. When they don’t, another version exists solely for the purpose of darker backgrounds.
Notice that even the colors change slightly to account for the darker background.
Therefore, whether we prepare a favicon manually or with a tool, we automatically pick the light-compatible logo and start with that. After all, desktop tabs are traditionally white or light gray. The problem arises when going dark

data.title: Calendars, Contacts and Files in Stalwart
data.author: gpi
data.article_summary: Stalwart v0.12 发布，从邮件服务器演变为完整的通信与协作平台。新版本引入日历、联系人和文件存储的原生支持，采用 CalDAV、CardDAV 和 WebDAV 标准，无需第三方集成。支持群组日历、共享地址簿和团队文件夹，并通过 WebDAV ACL 管理权限。改进的垃圾邮件过滤系统可自动学习信任联系人，减少误报。性能方面，优化了多节点环境下的缓存和反序列化，提升速度和效率。集群协调新增对 Eclipse Zenoh、Apache Kafka、Redpanda、NATS 和 Redis 的支持。未来版本将引入 CalDAV 调度、JMAP 扩展等功能，进一步提升协作体验。

不同观点：
• **对Stalwart开源性质的质疑**：
  - rossy指出Stalwart因FOSS许可问题从Arch包管理中删除，主要问题包括构建依赖专有代码以及web管理界面包含专有代码。这些“致命问题”未如开发者承诺的那样在数月内修复，导致无法升级。

  - lb_表示对Stalwart由单一开发者主导的担忧，担心该开发者如果放弃或消失，项目可能无法持续。

• **Stalwart的技术优势**：
  - matja认为Stalwart的内置集群功能和分布式数据库支持提供了高可用性选项，相比Dovecot在开源版本中无法实现完全高可用性，Stalwart是一个不错的选择。

  - hatzz对Stalwart主要开发者的匿名性表示怀疑，并指出无法找到有关Stalwart Labs公司的信息，认为开放性不足。

• **对Stalwart功能的赞赏**：
  - mjl-赞扬Stalwart的发布，特别是其集成了日历和地址簿功能，方便自建个人信息管理基础设施。

• **对项目方向的认可**：
  - pluto_modadic对Stalwart重新聚焦于邮件相关功能而非机器学习表示高兴。

• **对邮件去中心化的支持**：
  - FlamingMoe表示支持任何推动邮件去中心化的努力。

• **与其他软件的比较**：
  - throw_a_grenade质疑为何选择Stalwart而不是Nextcloud，后者拥有更大的应用生态系统。

• **对资助的认可**：
  - jazzyjackson对NLnet资助Stalwart表示赞赏。

争议焦点：Stalwart的开源性质及其开发者的透明度。部分用户对Stalwart的许可问题和开发者匿名性表示担忧，而其他用户则关注其技术优势和功能。

44103071.article_content:
We’re excited to announce the release of
Stalwart v0.12
, a significant milestone that evolves Stalwart from a powerful mail server into a complete, integrated
communication and collaboration platform
. This release delivers one of the most anticipated features from our community:
native support for calendars, contacts, and file storage
—all built directly into the server, with no need for third-party integrations.
Calendars, Contacts & Files – All in One Place
​
With v0.12, you no longer need to integrate third-party groupware solutions or run parallel systems to support collaboration. Stalwart now includes first-class support for
CalDAV calendars
,
CardDAV contacts
, and
WebDAV-based file storage
. This means users can manage their events, address books, and documents through any standards-compliant client, seamlessly connected to the same backend that handles their email.
Shared resources such as
group calendars
,
shared address books
, and
team-accessible file folders
are also fully supported, providing a robust foundation for collaboration without the need for external software or services. And, to support flexible collaboration, Stalwart includes full support for the
WebDAV Access Control List (ACL) extension
, enabling detailed, per-user and per-group permission management.
Improved Spam Filtering
​
Another thoughtful addition in this release is the integration of the spam filter with users’ personal address books. Messages from known or trusted contacts are now far less likely to be incorrectly flagged as spam. And if a legitimate message does get misclassified, the system automatically trains the
Bayesian classifier
to treat future similar messages as legitimate, improving accuracy over time without additional user intervention.
Performance Enhancements
​
Under the hood, Stalwart v0.12 introduces several key performance optimizations designed especially for
large, multi-node environments
. One of the most impactful changes is the introduction of
incremental caching
: Stalwart now keeps account metadata in memory and only fetches updates when something changes in the database. This significantly reduces load and speeds up response times.
Another major enhancement is the use of
zero-copy deserialization
. This means Stalwart can read data directly from memory buffers without copying it into new structures, lowering CPU usage and improving throughput. Combined with optimizations that reduce the number of required
database queries
for common operations, these changes result in a leaner, faster backend that scales much more efficiently.
While these gains may not be noticeable in smaller setups,
larger clusters and high-volume deployments will see noticeable performance improvements
.
Smarter and Faster Clustering
​
We’ve also made big strides in
cluster coordination
. Previously, Stalwart relied on a UDP-based gossip protocol that performed well but didn’t scale ideally under heavy workloads. With v0.12, cluster behavior is now adaptable based on deployment size.
In
small deployments
, Stalwart uses
Eclipse Zenoh
, a lightweight and efficient peer-to-peer pub/sub protocol. For
larger infrastructures
, you can now choose from robust, scalable backends like
Apache Kafka
,
Redpanda
,
NATS
, or
Redis
for handling inter-node coordination, state synchronization, and workload distribution.
Looking Ahead: What’s Next?
​
With Stalwart v0.12, we're delivering more than just features—we're delivering
freedom from fragmented infrastructure
. No more patching together third-party services to get the basics of collaboration working. Now, everything—
email, calendars, contacts, files, and sharing
—lives in a single, efficient, and secure system.
While v0.12 is a major leap forward, we’re already preparing additional enhancements for the next point release. In
v0.12.1
, you can expect support for
CalDAV Scheduling (RFC 6638)
, enabling automatic meeting invitations and attendee responses. We’re also adding support for
event notification alerts via email
, so users are always aware of upcoming events, even if they're not logged into their calendars.
Additionally, in the coming months, we will be releasing support for the
JMAP for Calendars
,
JMAP for Contacts
, and
JMAP for File Storage
extensions. JMAP offers a modern, efficient, and JSON-based alternative to legacy protocols, making it faster and easier to develop responsive, real-time collaboration tools. These additions will further streamline the user experience and reduce bandwidth and processing overhead across client-server interactions.
Thank you to everyone who contributed feedback, suggestions, and encouragement. We can’t wait to hear what you build with this release—and we’re just getting started.

  - lb_表示对Stalwart由单一开发者主导的担忧，担心该开发者如果放弃或消失，项目可能无法持续。

• **Stalwart的技术优势**：
  - matja认为Stalwart的内置集群功能和分布式数据库支持提供了高可用性选项，相比Dovecot在开源版本中无法实现完全高可用性，Stalwart是一个不错的选择。

• **对开发者匿名性的疑虑**：
  - hatzz对Stalwart主要开发者的匿名性表示怀疑，并指出无法找到有关Stalwart Labs公司的信息，认为开放性不足。

补充讨论：
• **对Stalwart功能的赞赏**：
  - mjl-赞扬Stalwart的发布，特别是其集成了日历和地址簿功能，方便自建个人信息管理基础设施。

• **对项目方向的认可**：
  - pluto_modadic对Stalwart重新聚焦于邮件相关功能而非机器学习表示高兴。

• **对邮件去中心化的支持**：
  - FlamingMoe表示支持任何推动邮件去中心化的努力。

• **与其他软件的比较**：
  - throw_a_grenade质疑为何选择Stalwart而不是Nextcloud，后者拥有更大的应用生态系统。

• **对资助的认可**：
  - jazzyjackson对NLnet资助Stalwart表示赞赏。

争议焦点：Stalwart的开源性质及其开发者的透明度。部分用户对Stalwart的许可问题和开发者匿名性表示担忧，而其他用户则关注其技术优势和功能。

data.author: Philpax

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对浏览器开发、功能更新及透明度的不同看法，特别是围绕Arc浏览器和Dia浏览器的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ko_pivot] 认为多空间（Space）功能是Arc浏览器的核心特色，但只有5.52%的日常活跃用户经常使用多空间，这让他感到惊讶。
• [WoodenChair] 对Dia浏览器从架构上优先考虑性能表示关注，特别是提到了停止使用TCA和SwiftUI，以保持Dia的轻量和快速响应，但对TCA是什么表示疑问。
• [rado] 喜欢垂直标签页功能，并希望该功能能在Safari甚至Chrome中出现。
• [tolerance] 对Arc浏览器开发者的态度持批评态度，认为其过于严肃且缺乏说服力。
• [twohaibei] 提到Arc浏览器在更新到manifest v3后，uBlock Origin插件无法使用，因此转向了Zen Browser。
• [nsonha] 没有使用Dia浏览器，但尝试过与Arc类似的Deta Surf浏览器，认为其AI集成更好，可以在同一个工作空间内引用标签页并与AI交流。
• [al_borland] 对Arc浏览器停止开发新功能并进入仅支持模式表示不满，认为缺乏透明度。他对文章中提到的“将软件维护得很好”持怀疑态度，认为浏览器需要持续进化，停留在安全更新和修复bug是不够的。他还指出，文章与实际行动的不一致性削弱了用户对开发者的信任。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Arc浏览器停止开发新功能的决定以及透明度问题。一些用户认为开发者没有充分告知用户这一决定，导致用户感觉被“欺骗”。
• 用户对Dia浏览器的性能改进表示关注，但对Arc浏览器的经验使得他们对Dia持保留态度。
• 实验性浏览器在市场中的作用被认为是积极的，因为它们为新想法提供了试验平台，即便最终是由大公司采纳这些想法。

整体来看，用户对浏览器开发的持续性、功能进化以及开发者的透明度有较高期望，并对实验性浏览器的市场定位提出质疑。

data.title: The dystopia of '1984' is already here
data.author: belter
data.article_summary: 导演劳尔·佩克（Raoul Peck）的新纪录片《奥威尔：2+2=5》在戛纳电影节首映，该片基于乔治·奥威尔的反乌托邦小说《1984》，探讨当今社会中权力对真相的压制。影片通过奥威尔的文本、信件、历史照片以及电影改编片段，结合当代监控社会和真理崩塌的现实，揭示了双重思想和思想罪等概念的当代体现。由演员达米安·刘易斯（Damian Lewis）旁白，影片不仅回顾了奥威尔的生平，还聚焦他生命最后阶段在苏格兰小岛上带病完成《1984》的决心。佩克结合自身在海地和扎伊尔的经历，强调公民抵抗极权的重要性，并通过展示当代政治人物如特朗普、普京等，警示法西斯主义的回潮。影片呼吁观众反思个人在世界中的角色和责任。

“How many fingers am I holding up?” Winston Smith, the protagonist of
1984
, answers based on what his eyes tell him: there are four. Only the Party agent directing his re-education insists that there are five. By dint of electric shocks and various forms of torture, he begins to doubt his own perception, until at the end of the book he also perceives them: there are five, no doubt about it. This passage from
George Orwell’s great dystopian novel
, in which truth yields to the pressure of power, gives rise to the new documentary by Raoul Peck, 71,
Orwell: 2+2 = 5
, presented in the Cannes Première section of the film festival.
That scene is the symbol that Peck has chosen to describe a society in which Orwell’s theses are no longer predictions of the future, but pure reality. His vision — based on concepts such as Big Brother, newspeak,
doublethink
, or thoughtcrime — crosses a present marked by constant surveillance, social fear, and the crumbling of the notion of truth. Narrated by actor Damian Lewis, the documentary interweaves Orwell’s texts and letters with archival photographs, fragments of the film adaptations of
1984
(one made 1956, with Edmund O’Brien, and another in 1984, with John Hurt), scenes from other films, from
Oliver Twist
to
Notting Hill
(!), and images taken from television and social networks.
For Orwell, every project began with a sense of injustice that he wanted to confront. For Peck, it’s no different. From his first short film, about Cuban troubadour Carlos Puebla’s visit to Cold War Berlin, to his films about James Baldwin (
I Am Not Your Negro
) or South African photographer Ernest Cole, which premiered at Cannes last year, his cinema has followed a clear and consistent political line.
“I come from Haiti. From very early on, I saw the hypocrisies of those who proclaim themselves defenders of democracy. And I am a Black person: I was confronted with societies that had decided that I had no right to exist,” says Peck on a terrace overlooking the port of Cannes.
Director Raoul Peck (l) and Damian Lewis attend the photocall for 'Orwell : 2+2Cine, Francia
CLEMENS BILAN (EFE)
Peck, who grew up under several liberticidal regimes — that of François Duvalier in Haiti, and that of Mobutu Sese Seko during his exile in Zaire — and saw his father imprisoned as an opponent, understood from an early age the importance of speaking out when everyone else is silent.
“As Orwell said: hope, if it exists, has to be built. It does not appear on its own. In the history of humanity, that has never worked. You resist, you organize, you make it happen. Authoritarian regimes, because they lose a war or a revolution breaks out. It may take five years or 30, but the same thing always happens: the system collapses or the citizens resist.”
In that sense, his film seems like a call to action. “It’s not my role, but I want every citizen to ask themselves: what am I doing in this world? At least, those who have the privilege to ask themselves that question. A child born in
s
outhern Congo
, working in a mine so you can have an iPhone, doesn’t have that choice. But maybe you do...”
More than an ordinary biography, the documentary recalls Orwell in the last years of his life. Sick with tuberculosis and isolated on a remote farm on the Scottish island of Jura, he was determined to finish
1984
before it was too late. His literary testament was published in 1949, just six months before his death.
Peck takes as his starting point the famous Party slogan that structures the novel: “War is peace. Freedom is slavery. Ignorance is strength.” And he makes it the instrument for examining how fascism threatens to make a comeback around the world. Through his images parade Putin, Netanyahu, Milei and Meloni, although the great protagonist is Donald Trump, of course, and his systematic disregard for the truth.
George Orwell.
Orwell was well-acquainted with the mechanisms of oppression. He observed them in Europe, fighting with the
International Brigades in the Spanish Civil War
, but he also exercised them: he was born in colonial India, son of a British official of the Opium Department, and worked for five years as an officer of the Imperial Police in Burma. Both experiences awakened in the writer a visceral rejection of authoritarianism and a deep sense of guilt.
He once wrote that, without the Empire, Britain would be no more than “a cold and unimportant little island where we should all have to work very hard and live mainly on herrings and potatoes,” another observation that already bordered on prophecy.
“One of the things that brought me closest to Orwell when I started reading him was the feeling that he seemed like someone from the Third World, like me. He seemed close to me, someone who understood me, like a brother,” says Peck, politicized in the left-wing circles of 1970s B

data.title: Non-Pointless Software Projects for New Devs in the LLM Age
data.author: Ameo
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在LLM（大型语言模型）时代，新手开发者如何选择有意义的软件项目来提升技能并展示能力。作者指出，许多常见的项目建议（如游戏克隆或脚本解释器）往往显得毫无实际用途，难以激发动力。作者建议开发者构建自己实际使用的项目，如截图托管和分享应用、提醒邮件CLI、Discord机器人、自托管的网络分析工具等。这些项目不仅能提高技术能力，还因为其实际用途而更有意义。作者以自己持续使用的截图应用为例，说明这种方法的长期价值，并鼓励开发者从简单项目开始，逐步添加功能，确保数据备份。这种方法不仅能增强学习动力，还能在求职时展示出更具实际意义的项目经验。

Webdev Slant
Conclusion + Philosophical Thoughts
I, like many other devs, learned most of my coding by building projects.  I've never been one to read textbooks or tutorials through chapter by chapter - I prefer to start something and then look stuff up along the way and trial-and-error my way to the end.
Building a portfolio of projects to show off your skills is still highly recommended to college-age devs trying to land their first job, judging by the posts on subreddits like /r/csMajors that show up on my Reddit homepage.
The issue is that it's often really hard to find an idea for a project to work on that feels worth doing.
I've heard this multiple times from friends learning software development, seen it echoed online, and experienced it myself.  It's easy to look up "software project ideas" online or ask ChatGPT to recommend something, but the many of those suggestions just seem so
pointless
.
Sure, building a snake game clone or writing your own tiny scripting language interpreter can be very educational and worthwhile.  But at the end of the project, the code's going to sit on Github and never get run by anyone again.  If you're lucky, some recruiter or dev assigned to be your interviewer will glance through the readme.
It's always been hard for me to find motivation to work on projects like that.  They felt like homework assignments without even the benefit of getting a good grade at the end if it turns out well.
In the age of AI coding, it's even worse.  Even if you don't use any LLM assistance, the knowledge that some LLM could generate the whole thing given a 50-word prompt is very demoralizing to say the least.
Non-Pointless Projects
I'll get straight to my point.
My solution for making projects feel like they matter is to build stuff that you use yourself
I've been programming and building software for over 10 years now.  Over that time, I've built many projects that I still use frequently.  The fact that they're real, living applications that actually serve a purpose automatically elevates them to be more meaningful that some artificial coding challenge.
Here are some of the things I've built over the years and use to this day:
Screenshot Hosting + Sharing App
One of the earliest projects I built was a webserver that I could upload screenshots to.  If you spend a lot of time online like me, then you probably post a lot of screenshots to apps like Discord or Slack.  For me at least, I still find it really cool to be able to post a link to a domain that's my username with a super-short URL.
You can make this as simple or complicated as you want.  Pretty much any tech stack in the world works for this.  You could do serverless, host it for free or virtually free, or drop it on a small VPS that you use as a base for all your other projects.  If you're in college, you can get the
Github Student Developer Pack
which comes with enough Digital Ocean credits to host a decent little VPS completely free.
If you use Windows, you can use the excellent
ShareX
desktop app to capture and upload screenshots with custom keyboard shortcuts.  I use Linux now which isn't supported, but back when I used ShareX I had multiple sets of shortcuts set up for different use cases.  One would upload a public image, one would be for one-time images that auto-delete after being viewed, one supported images that expired in a week, etc.
The other part of this which I only realized the value of later was the fact that I had a persistent, centralized collection of screenshots from all my computers going back years.
I built a little management web UI and can go back and scan through screenshots I took in the past.  The amount of memories and casual moments which would have been otherwise lost + forgotten is stunning.  I saw a blog post shared on Hacker News a couple of years ago titled
You should take more screenshots
which makes similar points to this and resonated with me deeply.
Anyway yeah I'm extremely glad I built this project, and it's one of the first things I'll recommend to people learning any kind of full stack or webdev stuff.

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了用户界面（UI）设计从扁平化向富有质感、深度和表现力的转变。作者Michael Flarup引用了Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky的观点，认为设计正回归色彩丰富和多维的风格，类似于iOS 7时期的变革。作者提出“Diamorph”一词来描述这种新风格，它强调深度、光影和层次，具有表现力和玩味性，区别于纯粹模仿现实物体的拟物设计（skeuomorphism）。文章还探讨了AI如何加速这种设计趋势，通过生成式AI工具，使得复杂的设计变得更容易实现，从而降低设计门槛。尽管AI生成设计仍有局限，但作者认为它能最大化创意，为新风格的普及提供助力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Airbnb redesign引发的关于UI设计趋势的讨论，涉及维度设计、UI一致性、设计美学与实用性之间的平衡等问题。

不同观点：
• **对Airbnb新设计的平淡反应**：[afavour] 对Airbnb的新设计感到失望，认为只是新图标，并没有实际的UI改进，不如Google的Material UI设计有趣。
• **支持设计中的趣味性**：[ketzo] 认为UI设计应该具有一定的趣味性，即使是细微的设计元素也能带来愉悦的体验，虽然“令人愉悦的UI”已成陈词滥调。
• **设计趋势的周期性**：[bitpush] 认为设计趋势如同时尚，具有周期性。当前的“维度设计”之后可能会被“激进的极简主义”取代。
• **实用性 vs 美学**：[1over137] 强调UI设计应基于可用性数据，而非仅仅美学考虑，批评让图形设计师主导设计决策。
• **对新旧设计混合的困惑**：[notnullorvoid] 指出Airbnb的新设计 inconsistent，部分图标是维度风格，而其他部分仍然是扁平设计，导致用户体验混乱。
• **LLM和四维设计趋势**：[dataviz1000] 认为当前的UI变化不仅仅是2D或3D，而是涉及到时间维度的变化（4D），LLM的输出不仅仅是屏幕上的反馈，而是自动化操作的实现。
• **对LLM和维度设计趋势的怀疑**：[nosefurhairdo] 怀疑Airbnb新设计能否代表真正的趋势，认为LLM使得设计维度更容易实现的说法不成立，因为高维度设计难以保持一致性。
• **怀旧与实用性冲突**：[taimurayaz] 和 [chank] 都提到当前设计趋势是怀旧驱动，但这种设计并不一定实用，过去的设计没有广泛流行，现在也可能不会。
• **对维度设计的美学批评**：[richardanaya] 认为新设计丑陋，更偏好Google的Material Design Expressive风格，认为其更具未来感。
• **对扁平设计的不满**：[recursivedoubts] 认为扁平化设计是灾难，希望通过AI和维度设计回归更具实用性的设计元素。
• **怀旧图标和设计风格**：[lxe] 和 [ookblah] 都表达了对早期21世纪图标和设计风格的怀念，认为当前设计趋势是历史的轮回。

补充讨论：
• **自然语言与自适应界面**：[choxi] 提出自然语言界面和自适应界面是未来的趋势，尤其是结合语言交流和自适应的用户体验，以及3D/VR/AR等技术在提高信息密度方面的潜力。

争议焦点：
• 设计趋势是否真正具有创新性，还是仅仅是历史的轮回。
• 新设计的美学价值与实用性之间的平衡，尤其是维度设计对一致性和用户体验的影响。
• LLM在UI设计中的作用以及其是否真的能带来设计上的改进。

Michael Flarup

Flat design is over. The future is colourful and dimensional.
Those aren’t my words. They’re
Brian Chesky’s
, CEO of Airbnb, after what can only be described as a landmark redesign of the platform. A redesign full of whimsical, animated, 3D icons and warm, tactile surfaces.
It’s always hard to pinpoint when a paradigm shift happens. Usually, you only recognize it in hindsight. iOS 7 in 2013 was one. These past few weeks have felt like another. The pendulum is swinging again.
Some of us worked toward this shift for years, so I’ll just say it:
We’re so back.
I told you so.
But if we’re really entering a new era of visual design, we need better language for it.
Redefining Dimensional Design
I’ve never liked the word
skeuomorphism
. A skeuomorph is when something digital borrows the concept of something physical—like a trash can icon that looks like a real bin, or a book app that flips pages like paper. But over time,
skeuomorphic
became a catch-all for any design with depth, texture, or lighting—and that’s a mistake. A bin icon, even as a flat glyph, is still a skeuomorph. It’s metaphor, not material.
I’ve been looking for a better word.
Something that captures the dimensionality we’re beginning to see.
Lately, I’ve been using the word
Diamorph
.
It’s not meant to be a grand rebrand of design. A completely invented word. A working title for a style that embraces depth, texture, and light. Not to mimic the real world, but to create something that feels native to the screen. Something expressive. Playful.
Diamorph
(adj.): dimensional design that embraces depth, light, texture, and hierarchy—native to the screen, expressive by intent.
Diamorphism
(n.): a growing tendency toward intentional dimensionality—layered, tactile, digital-first, and full of character.
Maybe it sticks. Maybe it doesn’t. But it’s been helpful for me to give this shift a name while we figure out where it’s heading.
If skeuomorphic design is performative, and flat design is reductive, maybe
Diamorph
is something else entirely—less about illusion, more about belonging.
Whatever you call it, it’s clear something is shifting. We’ve felt it building for a while: Big Sur icons, the many -phism experiments, playful micro-interactions, richer lighting models—it’s been building in waves. But now it’s breaking through.
And with it, we finally get to move past the tired flat-vs-skeuo binary. It’s time to make space for something new.
I won’t be surprised if WWDC in a couple of weeks introduces some kind of material injection into the digital surfaces Apple controls.
How AI Is Accelerating Diamorph Design
There’s also an interesting side story here, one that might help fuel the adoption of this new paradigm—and yes, you guessed it: AI.
After Airbnb showed off their redesign, the internet exploded with soft, dimensional, highly detailed icon sets prompted into existence using generative AI tools.
Back in the early 2000s, UI design like this had a high skill ceiling. It took years to master lighting, materials, and depth. Now? That level of craft is often just a prompt away.
I could mourn that—or I could celebrate the fact that the style I’ve championed for years is finally within reach for everyone.
In the end, I’ve always worked toward more fun and playful interfaces—and I think we’re about to see a lot more of them.
It’s surprisingly easy to get solid results when generating dimensional icons with AI. These retro consoles I grew up with were created using ChatGPT image prompts, then lightly cleaned up in Photoshop.
I’ve been crafting this style by hand for nearly two decades. These aren’t perfect, but they’re hitting the “good enough” mark for many use cases.
AI handles materials, lighting, and color surprisingly well. Perspective, proportions, and consistency across a set? Still a challenge. Most require a bit of artifact cleanup and a sanity check. (No, that’s not how a controller connects to a SNES.)
But with transparent backgrounds and a bit of finesse, they’re usable. Sometimes even production-ready. At the very least, they’re a strong base for further refinement.
It lowers the barrier to entry for this kind of design. I did a quick mockup of a game-collecting macOS app using these icons.
Here’s that mockup. And seriously—why don’t we have a great app for cataloguing physical media?
Like a lot of other artists, I have mixed feelings about the process. But I’ve always been pragmatic about tools. And if I treat AI as just that: a tool, not a shortcut to the final result—then there’s still a lot of room for craft, taste, and care.
In an ideal world, AI is a creativity maximiser. It lowers the bar but raises

data.title: The Network State
data.author: dp-hackernews
data.article_summary: 这本书探讨了利用技术创建“网络国家”（Network State）的可能性，网络国家被视为现行民族国家的后继者。书中首先简要介绍了网络国家的概念，并通过历史分析探讨了政治权力与技术进步的关系。接着，分析当前全球政治格局，特别是中美关系和技术发展趋势，讨论了去中心化和再中心化的未来。书中还详细对比了民族国家与网络国家的差异，并解释了为何现在是提出这一概念的时机。最后，附录部分提供了致谢和其他补充信息。本书旨在启发人们思考如何通过技术建立新的城市乃至国家。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：1729这个名字的象征意义及其与人才选拔的关联

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：评论者认同1729这个名字的象征意义，认为它代表了那些被传统体制忽视但拥有创新思想的人才。这种观点强调了发掘和支持有潜力但未被认可的人才的重要性，并与创建新型社会和网络国家的愿景相联系。

• 第二种观点：有些人可能会质疑这种命名是否过于理想化或抽象，认为仅凭一个数学常数来象征一种社会运动或人才选拔机制可能缺乏实际操作性。这种观点指出，实际发掘人才需要更具体的机制和标准，而不仅仅依赖于象征意义。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了"dark talent"（黑暗天赋）这一概念，意指那些未被主流认可但具有潜力的人才。这一概念引发了关于如何识别和支持这些人才的具体方法的讨论。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是1729这一数字的选择，因为它是拉马努金数（Ramanujan number），具有数学史上的特殊意义。对于一些了解其历史背景的人来说，这个数字能够激发一种浪漫主义的联想，但对于不了解其背景的人来说，可能难以引起共鸣。

• 争议的焦点可能在于，通过象征性的名字和概念是否真的能够有效地吸引和支持那些有创新思想的人才，还是需要更多实际的措施和制度来实现这一目标。

data.article_summary: 《Internet Archive》推出YouTube实时直播，展示微缩胶片（存储多份文档的胶片）的数字化过程。直播从周一至周五上午10:30至下午6:30进行，观众可以看到高分辨率相机拍摄胶片上的文档图像，并通过软件拼接和处理，最终上传至Internet Archive的公共数据库。该项目由App开发者Sophia Tung设立，并配有放松的Lo-Fi音乐。在非直播时段，观众还可以观看Internet Archive提供的其他内容，如公有领域的无声电影或NASA的历史图片。

不同观点：
• [ignoramous] 认为Cloudflare的验证码机制对网站存档造成了困难。他提到他所在的非正式组织致力于存档网站，但发现Cloudflare保护的网站几乎无法存档。他曾假设Cloudflare与Archive.org有合作，但似乎没有进展。

补充讨论：
• [ignoramous] 引用了Cloudflare的博客文章（https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflares-always-online-and-th...），可能暗示Cloudflare的"Always Online"功能和相关政策对网站存档造成了影响。
• 讨论中隐含的争议焦点在于Cloudflare的安全措施（如验证码）与网站存档需求之间的矛盾，特别是对于像Archive.org这样的存档项目而言。
• 未有直接反驳观点，但隐含的另一方观点可能是Cloudflare的验证码和其他安全措施对于保护网站免受自动化攻击和确保服务正常运行是必要的。

总结：讨论围绕Cloudflare验证码对网站存档的影响展开，一方认为其对存档工作造成了障碍，并期待与Archive.org的合作，而另一方可能强调安全措施的必要性。

44072137.article_content:
News
Now you can watch the Internet Archive preserve documents in real time
The feed offers a close-up look of how microfiche — the sheets of films that store multiple documents — are digitized and uploaded to the Archive.
The feed offers a close-up look of how microfiche — the sheets of films that store multiple documents — are digitized and uploaded to the Archive.
by
Emma Roth
May 22, 2025, 4:10 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Screenshot: The Verge
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
If you’ve ever wondered how the Internet Archive uploads all the physical documents on its site, now you can get a behind-the-scenes look at the process.
The Internet Archive launched
a new
YouTube livestream
that shows the digitization of microfiche in real time — complete with some relaxing, lo-fi beats.
Microfiche is a sheet of film that contains multiple images of miniaturized documents. It’s an old form of storing newspapers, court documents, government records, and other important documents. The Internet Archive uses these microfiche cards to digitize and upload documents to its online library.
The livestream shows a close-up look at one of the five microfiche digitization stations at the organization’s Richmond, California location, along with a look at the document that it’s working on. App maker Sophia Tung, who
created a LoFi music livestream showing
Waymo’s robotaxis returning to their parking lot, also
set up the microfiche livestream for the Internet Archive
.
“Operators feed microfiche cards beneath a high-resolution camera, which captures multiple detailed images of each sheet,” Chris Freeland, the Internet Archive’s director of library services, writes in a post on the site. “Software stitches these images together, after which other team members use automated tools to identify and crop up to 100 individual pages per card.”
From there, the Internet Archive processes the pages, makes them text-searchable, and then uploads them to its public collections.
The livestream runs from Monday through Friday from 10:30AM ET to 6:30PM ET. “During the day, you’ll see scanners working on custom machines to digitize all the microfiche in the world,” Tung says. “During the off hours, you can also see everything else that the Archive has to offer, like silent films in the public domain or historical pictures from NASA.”

data.title: Linux Cgroup from First Principles
data.author: setheron
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Linux的cgroup（控制组）概念，特别是cgroup v2。cgroup是一种将进程分组并限制其资源使用（如内存、CPU和网络带宽）的机制。自Linux内核4.5起，cgroup v2简化了设计，成为推荐版本。作者通过NixOS虚拟机演示如何创建和管理cgroup，所有cgroup都位于`/sys/fs/cgroup`目录下。通过创建目录和修改相关文件，用户可以设置资源限制和查看进程状态。例如，通过修改`memory.max`文件限制内存使用。作者建议逐步学习，先从一个资源限制开始，再逐步理解整个系统。文中还提供了示例代码以帮助理解。

44102958.article_content:
Linux cgroup from first principles
Published 2025-05-26 on
Farid Zakaria's Blog
After having spent the better part of 2 weeks learning Linux’s cgroup (control group) concept, I thought I better write this down for the next brave soul. 🦸
Facebook’s cgroup2
microsite
is also a fantastic resource. I highly recommend reading it 🤓.
Let’s dive in and learn
cgroup
, specifically
cgroup v2
.
There is a distinction between v2 and v1 implementation of cgroup.  However v2 was introduced in Linux kernel 4.5 in 2016. It included a much simpler design, so we will consider it the only version to simplify this guide
[ref]
.
As a quick aside, what I love about Linux is the Unix design philosophy
“everything is a file”
. This bleeds itself into everything in Linux especially on how to interface with various kernel subsystems.
While higher-level tools and libraries often abstract these direct file manipulations,
If you can
read
and
write
to a file, you can communicate with the kernel! 📜
Linux control groups are a sort of container you can place processes within and apply a variety of limits on resources allocations such as: memory, cpu and network bandwidth.
We will be using the following NixOS VM to build and run this guide if you want to follow along.
vm.nix
let
# release-24.11
nixpkgs
=
fetchTarball
"https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/archive/5ef6c425980847c78a80d759abc476e941a9bf42.tar.gz"
;
nixos
=
import
"
${
nixpkgs
}
/nixos"
{
configuration
=
{
modulesPath
,
pkgs
,
...
}:
{
imports
=
[
(
modulesPath
+
"/virtualisation/qemu-vm.nix"
)
];
virtualisation
=
{
graphics
=
false
;
};
users
.
users
.
alice
=
{
isNormalUser
=
true
;
extraGroups
=
[
"wheel"
];
packages
=
with
pkgs
;
[
file
libcgroup
vim
(
pkgs
.
runCommandCC
"throttled"
{
src
=
pkgs
.
writeText
"throttled.c"
''
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <time.h>
static long long now_ns() {
struct timespec ts;
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
return (long long)ts.tv_sec * 1000000000LL + ts.tv_nsec;
}
int main() {
long long last = now_ns();
int count = 0;
while (1) {
count++;
if (count % 1000000 == 0) {
long long current = now_ns();
long long delta_ms = (current - last) / 1000000;
printf("Delta: %lld ms\n", delta_ms);
fflush(stdout);
last = current;
}
}
return 0;
}
''
;
}
''
mkdir -p $out/bin
$CC -o $out/bin/throttled $src
''
)
(
pkgs
.
runCommandCC
"hog"
{
src
=
pkgs
.
writeText
"hog.c"
''
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
int main() {
while (1) {
char *mem = malloc(1024 * 1024);
if (!mem) {
perror("malloc");
break;
}
memset(mem, 1, 1024 * 1024);
printf("1 MB allocated\n");
fflush(stdout);
sleep(1);
}
return 0;
}
''
;
}
''
mkdir -p $out/bin
$CC -o $out/bin/hog $src
''
)
];
initialPassword
=
""
;
};
security
.
sudo
.
wheelNeedsPassword
=
false
;
services
.
getty
.
autologinUser
=
"alice"
;
system
.
stateVersion
=
"24.11"
;
};
};
in
nixos
.
vm
Although a single
cgroup
can enforce multiple resource allocations, we will do so one at a time to simplify.
All
cgroup
live beneath the special directory
/sys/fs/cgroup
directory, which is referred to as the
root cgroup
.
You can inspect your login shells current cgroup by inspecting
/proc/self/cgroup
The returned value is what should be appended to the root.
>
cat
/proc/self/cgroup
0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/session-5.scope
>
file /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/session-5.scope
/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/session-5.scope: directory
If you are confused with the
slice
and
scope
stuff in the path just ignore that 🤔. That is a
systemd
concept to help organize cgroups.
Let’s create a simple hierarchy we want for the purpose of learning.
In practice you will probably have these groups created to model the business domain or the various processes you want to group together and not the controllers you want to express.
/sys/fs/cgroup
└── demo/
├── cpu-limited/
├── memory-limited/
└── network-limited/
Since “everything is a file” is the mantra of our Linux API, let’s just
mkdir
the groups.
sudo mkdir
/sys/fs/cgroup/demo
sudo chown
-R
$USER
/sys/fs/cgroup/demo
mkdir
/sys/fs/cgroup/demo/cpu-limited
mkdir
/sys/fs/cgroup/demo/memory-limited
mkdir
/sys/fs/cgroup/demo/network-limited
If we look inside a single cgroup, we see a bunch of virtual files.
ls
-1
/sys/fs/cgroup/demo |
head
cgroup.controllers
cgroup.events
cgroup.freeze
cgroup.kill
cgroup.max.depth
cgroup.max.descendants
cgroup.subtree_control
...
memory.low
memory.max
memory.min
memory.numa_stat
memory.oom.group
memory.peak
...
network-limited
pids.current
pids.events
pids.max
pids.peak
Some of these files help set the value on the various controllers such as
memory.max
which sets the absolute aggregate maximum memory all processes either attached to this cgroup or any of its descendants can allocate.
Other files, give you live accounting information or events such as
memory.current
or
memory.events
.
All the files that begin with
cgroup
itself, help set up the cgroup and turn on/o

data.title: Lottie is an open format for animated vector graphics
data.author: marcodiego
data.article_summary: Lottie是一种开源的矢量图形动画文件格式，由Hernan Torrisi于2015年创建，最初用于从Adobe After Effects导出和播放动画。Lottie动画通常包含复杂的动画、动态图形和交互元素，并可以导出为JSON文件，该文件包含重建动画所需的所有信息，如关键帧和图层信息。Lottie基于JSON格式，具有开放性、易于传输和使用现有工具进行操作的特点。Lottie动画社区（LAC）是一个由Linux基金会托管的非营利开源项目，致力于推动Lottie格式成为高效、可扩展和跨平台的动画技术标准。LAC通过开放协作，促进Lottie格式的广泛采用和标准化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lottie动画格式的优缺点及替代方案

不同观点：
• **Lottie的缺点和性能问题**：panstromek指出Lottie的JSON格式导致文件过大，加载和解析过程复杂，尤其在网页上表现不佳，浏览器在处理多个动画时性能较差。Tade0和lwansbrough也提到在使用Lottie时遇到性能问题，特别是在低端设备上。
• **Lottie与SVG/CSS动画的比较**：herrherrmann认为Lottie相对于SVG和CSS动画过于臃肿，且官网宣传具有误导性。使用CSS和SVG可以获得更小、更易调整的动画。
• **Lottie与Rive的比较**：lwansbrough和zdragnar提到Rive在解决Lottie问题上的优势，特别是在动态数据更新和性能方面，Rive可能是更好的选择。
• **Lottie的实用性和工作流**：nye2k认为Lottie在多种平台和工作流中整合良好，尤其是在After Effects之后替代Flash的工作中，具有多种优势。b3ing则指出Rive在艺术创作方面不如Lottie直观。

补充讨论：
• **Lottie的压缩和优化**：gervwyk提到Lottie动画的导出文件过大，需使用专有工具进行压缩，这增加了成本。
• **Lottie的替代工具**：rogierhofboer介绍了一些未提及的工具如Google Web Designer和Expressive Animator，其中一些支持Lottie格式。
• **Lottie的维护和开发**：ComputerGuru提到AirBnb已放弃Lottie，可能影响其未来发展。
• **其他格式和历史背景**：userbinator和nokeya讨论了SWF格式的效率和可用性，以及rlottie库的使用。
• **生成矢量动画的最新技术**：zhyder关注生成矢量动画的最新技术，指出当前文本生成模型和图像扩散模型在矢量图形生成方面的不足。
• **LottieFiles团队的工作**：sandra_vu提到LottieFiles团队在优化Lottie格式和工作流方面的努力。

争议焦点：Lottie格式在网页和低端设备上的性能问题，及其相对于SVG和CSS动画的臃肿性。同时，Rive作为替代方案的优劣也在讨论中被提及。

44088216.article_content:
Lottie is an open format for animated vector graphics
​​Lottie is an open-source vector graphics animation file format. It was first created in 2015 by Hernan Torrisi as an export format for the export and playback of animations from Adobe After Effects. It is now a highly popular animation format used on the web, mobile applications and other systems with multiple independent renderer implementations and creation support.
Read the Spec
Contribute
What is Lottie?
Lottie animations are typically created using Adobe After Effects, and they can include complex animations, motion graphics, and interactive elements. Once an animation is created, it can be exported as a Lottie JSON file. This JSON file contains all the information needed to recreate the animation, including keyframes, easing curves, and layer information.
Vector Graphics
Vector Graphics are resolution-independent images created from geometric shapes like curves and lines rather than a grid of pixels
Tweening
Tweening is the process of animating graphics where the animator defines shape properties at specific keyframes and the frames between those are interpolated automatically.
Rich Ecosystem
A mature and robust ecosystem of players, creation tools, libraries and free assets. Trusted and used by thousands of companies to enrich their user experience.
Open file format
Lottie is an open standard based on the JSON format, allowing for ease of transfer over the web and manipulation with existing tools.
Read the Spec
About Lottie Animation Community
Lottie Animation Community (LAC), a non-profit open source project hosted by The Linux Foundation, dedicated to establishing the Lottie File Format as an efficient, scalable and cross-platform animated vector graphics technology and open file format.
LAC was founded by a community of pioneers in recognition of that need. LAC aims to develop a formal Lottie format specification for implementation across renderers and other tools, and works towards the promotion and widespread adoption of the Lottie file format as an industry standard.
LAC operates as a project under the governance of the Joint Development Foundation, guaranteeing an open, collaborative approach to our standardization efforts. Our work is deeply rooted in transparency, ensuring that everyone in our community has a voice in the development and refinement of the Lottie File Format.
Contribute

• **生成矢量动画的最新技术**：zhyder关注生成矢量动画的最新技术，指出当前文本生成模型和图像扩散模型在矢量图形生成方面的不足。
• **LottieFiles团队的工作**：sandra_vu提到LottieFiles团队在优化Lottie格式和工作流方面的努力。

data.title: Scaling RNNs to Billions of Parameters with Zero Order
data.author: fchaubard
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种利用零阶优化（Zero-Order Optimization, ZOO）方法来训练大规模循环神经网络（RNNs）的技术。与依赖反向传播（BPTT）的传统方法不同，ZOO方法如随机向量梯度估计（RGE）在训练过程中不需要保存中间激活值，从而大幅降低内存消耗。实验表明，这种方法可以在多个任务上达到或超过BPTT的训练效果，尤其是在长上下文场景中表现更优。此外，中心差分RGE（CD-RGE）通过优化平滑替代损失，进一步提升了模型的泛化能力。尽管每步需要更多前向传递，但通过现代分布式推理技术，整体训练时间仍可优于BPTT。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否可以用RNN替代Transformer模型，以及相关算法和内存效率的比较

不同观点：
• fchaubard认为Transformer模型在推理过程中会保留所有之前的token，导致巨大的GPU内存消耗和成本，而人类的大脑则通过类似于分页的方式，只保留重要的信息。相比之下，RNN更像人类，因为它们将之前的token压缩成一个小的固定大小的内存。然而，传统的通过时间反向传播（BPTT）算法无法有效扩展，且存在梯度爆炸和消失的问题。

• fchaubard提出了一种1992年的零阶算法来替代BPTT，并声称这种算法不仅能很好地扩展，而且在某些情况下训练速度比BPTT快19倍。这暗示了RNN可能通过这种新算法重新成为主流，甚至替代Transformer。

补充讨论：
• 内存效率问题：Transformer模型在生成每个新token时需要保留所有之前的token，导致内存占用巨大，而RNN通过压缩信息进入固定大小的内存，内存效率更高。

• 算法扩展问题：传统的BPTT算法无法有效扩展，存在梯度爆炸和消失的问题，而新发现的零阶算法解决了这些问题，并且在训练速度上表现出色。

• RNN替代Transformer的潜力：如果RNN能够通过新的算法在性能上超越或至少接近Transformer，那么RNN有可能重新成为一种主流模型架构。

争议焦点：RNN是否真的能够通过新的算法在实际应用中替代Transformer，尤其是在性能和可扩展性方面。这需要更多的实验和验证。

Computer Science > Machine Learning

Title:
Scaling Recurrent Neural Networks to a Billion Parameters with Zero-Order Optimization
Authors:
Francois Chaubard
,
Mykel Kochenderfer
View a PDF of the paper titled Scaling Recurrent Neural Networks to a Billion Parameters with Zero-Order Optimization, by Francois Chaubard and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
During inference, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) scale constant in both FLOPs and GPU memory with increasing context length, as they compress all prior tokens into a fixed-size memory. In contrast, transformers scale linearly in FLOPs and, at best, linearly in memory during generation, since they must attend to all previous tokens explicitly. Despite this inference-time advantage, training large RNNs on long contexts remains impractical because standard optimization methods depend on Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT). BPTT requires retention of all intermediate activations during the forward pass, causing memory usage to scale linearly with both context length and model size. In this paper, we show that Zero-Order Optimization (ZOO) methods such as Random-vector Gradient Estimation (RGE) can successfully replace BPTT to train RNNs with convergence rates that match, or exceed BPTT by up to 19 fold, while using orders of magnitude less memory and cost, as the model remains in inference mode throughout training. We further demonstrate that Central-Difference RGE (CD-RGE) corresponds to optimizing a smoothed surrogate loss, inherently regularizing training and improving generalization. Our method matches or outperforms BPTT across three settings: (1) overfitting, (2) transduction, and (3) language modeling. Across all tasks, with sufficient perturbations, our models generalize as well as or better than those trained with BPTT, often in fewer steps. Despite the need for more forward passes per step, we can surpass BPTT wall-clock time per step using recent advancements such as FlashRNN and distributed inference.

data.article_summary: Expressive Animator 是一款可让用户轻松创建惊艳 SVG 动画的工具，支持 Windows 和 macOS，一次性付费永久使用。它提供强大的矢量图形编辑和动画功能，支持从 Figma、PDF 和 Adobe Illustrator 导入文件，并通过关键帧、缓动编辑器、运动路径等工具实现精确控制。用户可自定义画板大小，利用渐变、滤镜、混合模式等效果提升设计，并导出为视频、GIF、动画 SVG 等多种格式。该工具还提供完整的字体控制和高效的设计辅助功能，帮助用户制作令人难忘的社交媒体内容和网页设计。

主要讨论点：用户对一款非传统俄罗斯方块游戏的反馈和建议

不同观点：
• [hnlmorg] 认为游戏的随机方块生成可能存在问题，建议采用"single bag system"以减少特定方块长时间不出现的概率，从而降低游戏压力。
• [xnickb] 提到游戏可以帮助练习预判能力，但需要能看到接下来的几个方块。同时，他认为这款游戏比传统俄罗斯方块更放松。
• [lynx97] 分享了自己为盲文显示器用户开发的横向俄罗斯方块游戏，并提供了项目链接，展示了针对特殊用户群体的创新玩法。
• [irjustin] 提到自己尝试进行“全屏”挑战，虽然试图增加难度，但最终还是感受到压力，与游戏原本的放松设计初衷相悖。
• [lorikmor] 起初觉得游戏无聊，但后来喜欢上了这种不带来压力的玩法，认为这是一个有趣的概念。

补充讨论：
• [bramvanleur] 建议加入“撤销”功能，让方块可以从掉落位置重新调整，并希望游戏能根据玩家行为提供专业建议，帮助玩家提升技巧。
• [hansmayer] 开玩笑地建议加入MCP接口，让AI代替玩家进行游戏。
• [filt] 认为增加“幽灵方块”功能会有帮助，让玩家更直观地看到方块的落点。
• [metayrnc] 称赞游戏在移动设备上的操作体验非常好，没有常见的触摸屏操作问题。
• [aronhegedus] 提到自己在游戏开始时连续获得了多个“I”方块，以为游戏是某种特定方块变体。

data.article_summary: Clojure MCP 是一个处于早期开发阶段的 Alpha 软件，旨在通过 AI 辅助实现 Clojure 项目的 REPL 驱动开发。它提供一个 MCP 服务器，连接 AI 模型与 Clojure nREPL，并集成专用 Clojure 编辑工具，提升开发效率。主要功能包括 Clojure REPL 连接、Clojure 感知编辑（使用 clj-kondo、parinfer 等工具）、以及为 Clojure 开发优化的工具集。该项目强调即时反馈、增量开发、人工监督和函数式编程。安装需配置 Clojure、Java、Claude Desktop 等环境，并将 MCP 服务器与 nREPL 连接。项目可在本地运行，但目前需共享文件系统。用户可通过配置文件接入 Claude Desktop 实现 AI 辅助开发。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

Clojure MCP - REPL-Driven Development with AI Assistance
⚠️
Alpha Software - Work in Progress
This project is in early development and rapidly evolving. While I've found it invaluable for working with Clojure projects and it has significantly improved my development workflow, expect breaking changes, rough edges, and incomplete documentation.
🤝 Help Wanted!
If you find this useful, please consider contributing:
Report bugs and issues you encounter
Suggest improvements or new features
Submit pull requests for fixes or enhancements
Share your configuration patterns and workflows
Help improve documentation and examples
Your feedback and contributions will help make this tool better for the entire Clojure community!
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Clojure that provides a
complete set of tools to aid in the development of Clojure projects.
🚀 Overview
This project implements an MCP server that connects AI models to a
Clojure nREPL, and Specialized Clojure editing tools enabling a unique
Clojure develop experience.
Clojure MCP provides a superset of the tools that Claude Code uses,
so you can use it to work on Clojure
without any other tools
.  I
highly recommend using it with Claude Desktop to start.  It's
prettier and there are
no api charges!
Claude Desktop also let's you
have quick access to
your own prompts
and other resources provided
by the clojure-mcp server. Having a stack of your own prompts
available in a UI menu is pretty nice.
Main Features
Clojure REPL Connection
Clojure Aware editing
- Using clj-kondo, parinfer, cljfmt, and clj-rewrite
Optimized set of tools for Clojure Development
superset of Claude Code
Emacs edit highlighting
- alpha
Why REPL-Driven Development with AI?
This approach enables:
Immediate feedback
- Validate code by running it in a stateful REPL, not just statically analyzing it
Incremental development
- Build solutions in small, verified steps
Human oversight
- Keep the programmer in the loop for guidance
Functional approach
- Encourage pure functions that are easier to understand and test
📋 Installation
Prerequisites
Clojure
(1.11 or later)
Java
(JDK 11 or later)
Claude Desktop
(for the best experience)
Setting up the project
Step 1: Get the Clojure MCP Server
Clone this repository to your development machine
git clone https://github.com/bhauman/clojure-mcp.git
or use it as git dep in your

data.title: GitHub MCP exploited: Accessing private repositories via MCP
data.author: andy99
data.article_summary: 文章披露了GitHub MCP服务器的一个严重漏洞，该漏洞允许攻击者通过恶意GitHub Issue劫持用户代理，窃取私有代码库的数据。这一漏洞由Invariant的安全分析工具发现，属于首次发现的“有毒代理流”（Toxic Agent Flows）类型。攻击者可在公共代码库中创建恶意问题，当用户查询代理时触发数据泄露，将私有信息暴露在公开的代码库中。文章详细描述了攻击步骤、演示了具体案例，并提出了检测和缓解此类攻击的方法。这一漏洞提醒业界在部署编码代理和集成开发环境时需提高安全意识。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLM（如Claude）在使用GitHub访问令牌时的潜在安全问题和漏洞的讨论

不同观点：
• **losvedir**：认为用户在给LLM提供凭证时应该意识到该凭证的权限范围。如果使用细粒度的访问令牌，限制其仅能访问必要的资源，这种攻击不会成功。攻击的成功依赖于LLM拥有全局访问权限，这是危险的。
• **mirzap**：不认为这是一种“ exploit（漏洞利用）”。如果给代理提供了一个访问私有仓库的令牌，那么它就可以访问该仓库。问题的关键在于权限设置，而不是工具本身的漏洞。
• **kiitos**：认为有关漏洞的声明被夸大了。问题的发生需要多个条件同时满足，包括用户设置不当等。这并不完全是系统漏洞，更多是用户配置不当导致。
• **adeon**：从安全角度出发，认为如果LLM处理来自不可信来源的文本，该来源可能引导LLM生成任意文本并调用工具，因此存在风险。同时，指出需要外部安全产品来加强AI系统的安全性，表明AI公司在安全设计上不足。
• **godelski**：认为问题核心在于用户将敏感信息交给了不可信的第三方。这更像是一个用户错误，而非系统漏洞。同时质疑将未成熟的AI技术用于对安全有高要求的场景是否合适。
• **ttoinou**：建议用户可以精细控制LLM对自身信息的访问权限，并希望通过软件硬性限制而不是依赖LLM的模糊描述来保障安全。
• **drkrab**：指出当用户给第三方访问GitHub仓库时，也必须信任该第三方遵循所有安全策略，这实际上很难完全保证。
• **TOMDM**：认为问题类似于将私人信息暴露给公众然后惊讶于信息泄露。如果不希望LLM访问某些私人信息，就不应给予其访问权限。
• **ed**：不认为这是攻击，因为Claude只是按照要求执行任务。建议GitHub考虑引入人工审核机制以防止意外泄露。

补充讨论：
• **mcintyre1994**：对LLM提到的“排除minesweeper”感到好奇，并怀疑是否存在一个私有仓库与此相关。
• **lbeurerkellner**：分享了一个具体的恶意issue链接，展示LLM如何被引导完成利用。
• **pawanjswal**：对一个简单的GitHub issue能导致私有仓库数据泄露表示惊讶。
• **kapitanjakc**：分享了GitHub Copilot之前也存在读取私有仓库的经历，表明类似问题早已存在。

争议焦点：
• 该问题是否应被视为系统漏洞还是用户配置错误。
• LLM处理不可信输入时的潜在风险以及是否需要外部安全产品来增强安全性。
• 是否应在安全敏感场景中使用尚未成熟的AI技术。
